Many children and parents walk past
1.e: Shops do well where lots of their customers pass by.

1.q: What is a customer's 'complaint'?
o: Telling the shop something was wrong
1.e: If a toy is broken when you buy it, you can complain and ask the shop to fix or change it.

1.q: Which shop sells medicine?
1.e: A pharmacy sells medicines, often with a pharmacist to help.

1.q: A bridge is closed for repairs. What happens to delivery trucks?
o: They take a longer road around
1.e: A closed bridge means detours - deliveries take longer and cost more fuel.

1.q: Why do shopkeepers smile and say thank you?
o: It is a rule of maths
1.e: Good service makes customers want to return - that keeps a shop in business.

1.q: Which of these is a service, not a thing you take home?
1.e: A service is work someone does for you, like cutting hair or fixing a bike.

1.q: A shop gives a free balloon with each pair of shoes. Why?
o: To make customers happy and choose that shop
1.e: Small gifts encourage customers to buy from that shop.

1.q: You make 10 paper flowers and sell 6. How many are still for sale?
1.e: 10 - 6 = 4 flowers.

1.q: What is a factory?
o: A place where things are made in large numbers
1.e: Factories use machines and workers to make many products, like cars or biscuits.

1.q: Which is the right order for a biscuit?
o: Factory makes it, truck delivers it, shop sells it, you eat it
You eat it, factory makes it
Shop makes it, factory eats it
1.e: Goods travel along a chain: made, moved, sold, used.

1.q: What does 'free delivery' mean?
o: The shop brings it to you without charging for the trip
1.e: You still pay for the item, but not for bringing it to your home.

1.q: Why do sellers keep their stalls clean and tidy?
o: Customers like buying from clean places
1.e: A clean, tidy stall looks trustworthy and attracts buyers.

1.q: A fisherman catches 30 fish and sells them all at Rs 2 each. How much does he get?
Which helps you know if a shop is selling at a fair price?
o: Pay whatever they say without looking
1.e: Comparing prices helps you find a fair deal.

1.q: A toll booth on a bridge collects money from drivers. Is this buying a thing or a service?
1.e: Tolls pay for the service of crossing safely on a well-kept bridge.

1.q: Why might a shop close down?
o: It has too many happy customers
Not enough customers buy from it
1.e: If a shop earns less than it spends, it cannot keep going.

1.q: A sign says 'Buy 1, get 1 free'. You want 2 juice boxes at Rs 10. How much do you pay?
1.e: Pay for 1 (Rs 10) and get the second free.

1.q: Who decides the price of things in a shop?
o: The shopkeeper, thinking about costs and what buyers will pay
1.e: Sellers set prices to cover their costs and earn a little, while staying fair for buyers.

1.q: Why do toy adverts often appear during children's TV shows?
o: Because children watching are the people they want to reach
1.e: Companies show adverts where their buyers are watching. Clever - so think before you ask for it!

1.q: A market stall sells 5 coconuts in the morning and 7 in the afternoon. How many in the day?
1.e: 5 + 7 = 12 coconuts.

1.q: What is a 'shopping trolley' for?
o: Carrying the things you want to buy around the shop
1.e: A trolley holds your items while you shop - easier than carrying everything!

1.q: Why do farmers sell more vegetables at harvest time?
o: They have lots of fresh crops ready
1.e: At harvest time supply is high, so markets are full and prices are often lower.

1.q: Which job helps goods cross a river where there is no bridge?
1.e: Ferries carry people and goods across water. A bridge does the same job every minute of the day.

1.q: You open a stall and nobody comes. What could you try?
o: Make a bright sign and tell people
1.e: Letting people know you exist is the first step of any business.

1.q: What does 'cash' mean?
o: Notes and coins you can hold
1.e: Cash is physical money. People can also pay with cards or phones.

1.q: Which can people use to pay instead of cash?
o: A bank card or a phone app
1.e: Cards and phone apps move money from your bank account to the shop's.

1.q: A shop orders 40 notebooks and sells 25. How many are left in stock?
1.e: 40 - 25 = 15 notebooks.

1.q: Why is honesty important for a shopkeeper?
o: Customers trust honest shops and return
1.e: Fair weights and true prices build trust - and trust brings customers back.

1.q: A scale in a shop is used to...
o: Weigh goods like rice and vegetables
1.e: Shops weigh loose goods so you pay for exactly the amount you get.

1.q: Rice costs Rs 40 per kg. How much for 2 kg?
What is a 'shop assistant'?
o: A person who helps customers in a shop
1.e: Shop assistants help you find things, answer questions and take payment.

1.q: Why do shops sell umbrellas at the door on rainy days?
o: People suddenly need them when it rains
1.e: Selling what people need right now, right where they see it, is smart business.

1.q: A train carries 10 wagons of coal to a power station. What is this called?
1.e: Moving goods by train, truck or ship is called freight. MODIS BridgeWorks Levels 2, 4 and 9 are all about freight!

1.q: You sell cookies at Rs 3 each and sell 4. Your ingredients cost Rs 5. How much did you earn after costs?
1.e: Money in: 4 x 3 = 12. Minus costs 5: Rs 7 profit.

1.q: What does a 'Closed' sign on a shop door mean?
o: You cannot buy there right now
The shop has moved to the moon
1.e: Closed means the shop is not serving customers at the moment.

1.q: A toy has a 'Made in Japan' label. What does it tell you?
1.e: Labels show where goods were made. Many goods travel across the world before reaching you.

1.q: Which is the best way to carry home many groceries?
1.e: A strong bag carries more and can be used again and again.

1.q: Why are some foods sold in tins or packets?
o: To keep them fresh and safe for longer
1.e: Packaging protects food from air, dirt and germs so it lasts longer.

1.q: What does the 'best before' date on food tell you?
o: Until when the food is at its best
1.e: After that date the food may not taste as good. Always check it!

1.q: A shop sells 3 kinds of ice cream. Another sells 10 kinds. Why might people prefer the second?
1.e: More choice helps customers find exactly what they like.

1.q: Two shops sell the same bread. One is far, one is near. Both cost Rs 30. Which do you choose?
o: The near one - same price, less walking
1.e: When price and quality are the same, convenience decides.

1.q: A bridge lets farmers reach the town market in 10 minutes instead of 1 hour. What happens to their business?
o: They can sell more and keep food fresher
1.e: Faster trips mean fresher produce, more trips and more sales - bridges help whole towns grow.

1.q: What is a 'stall'?
o: A small open shop, often in a market
1.e: Market stalls are small shops set up on tables or carts.

1.q: Your stall sells pencils at Rs 4. A friend's stall sells the same for Rs 3. What might customers do?
1.e: Customers often choose the lower price for the same thing. That is called competition.

1.q: What is a 'customer queue number'?
o: A number that shows whose turn it is
1.e: Ticket numbers keep busy counters fair: everyone is served in order.

1.q: A lorry carries 100 boxes and delivers 20 at each shop. How many shops can it fill?
1.e: 100 shared into groups of 20: 5 shops.

1.q: Why do sellers weigh fruit in front of you?
o: So you can see it is fair
1.e: Weighing openly shows you get what you pay for.

1.q: Which is a good name for a shop that sells shoes?
1.e: A good shop name tells people what it sells.

1.q: A shop is always crowded at 5 pm. What could the shopkeeper do?
1.e: More helpers at busy times keep queues short and customers happy.

1.q: What is a 'shopping list' for?
1.e: A list helps you buy what you need and avoid forgetting - or overspending.

1.q: A shop sells a cake for Rs 50 that cost Rs 40 to make. What is its profit?
1.e: Profit = selling price - cost = 50 - 40 = Rs 10.

1.q: What happens if a shop sells a cake for less than it cost to make?
1.e: Selling below cost is a loss. Shops cannot do that for long.

1.q: A town gets a new bridge. Shops on the far side get...
o: More customers from across the river
1.e: Bridges connect people to shops, so trade grows on both sides.

1.q: Who checks that shop scales are honest?
1.e: Inspectors test scales so that 1 kg in every shop really is 1 kg.

1.q: A child sells old toys at a garage sale. What is the child doing?
1.e: Selling things you no longer need is a small business - and helps someone else get a bargain.

1.q: Which is a 'customer'?
o: A person buying vegetables at a stall
1.e: The customer is the person who buys.

1.q: Why do shops display prices clearly?
o: So customers can decide quickly and trust the shop
1.e: Clear prices make shopping easy and fair.

1.q: A truck can carry 10 sacks per trip. How many trips for 30 sacks?
1.e: 30 shared into 10s: 3 trips. Planning trips saves fuel and time.

1.q: What is a 'shop window' display for?
o: Showing goods to people walking past
1.e: A nice window display invites passers-by to come in.

1.q: If a shop doubles its price, what might happen to how many people buy?
1.e: Higher prices usually mean fewer buyers. Sellers must find a fair balance.

1.q: What is 'trade' between two towns?
o: Buying and selling goods between them
1.e: Towns trade: one sells rice, the other sells cloth. Roads and bridges make it possible.

1.q: A potter makes 6 pots a day and sells them all. How many pots in 5 days?
1.e: 6 x 5 = 30 pots - steady work builds a business.

1.q: Why do toll bridges show their prices on a big board before the booth?
o: So drivers know the charge before they arrive
1.e: Clear prices in advance are fair to customers - drivers can decide to pay or take another road.

1.q: What does a bridge do?
o: It helps us cross over water or a road
1.e: A bridge is a path that lets you walk or drive over something you cannot normally cross, like a river.

1.q: Which shape is used most in bridges to hold weight?
1.e: Engineers love the triangle because all three sides push against each other so it never changes shape under a load.

1.q: What do we call the tall posts that hold up a bridge's cables?
1.e: The tall vertical posts of a cable bridge are called towers or pylons. The cables hang from them.

1.q: What is a bridge made of that is very hard and shiny?
1.e: Steel is a very strong, hard metal used for beams and cables in modern bridges.

1.q: A bridge must be strong enough to hold cars and trucks. What word means 'how much weight something can hold'?
1.e: Load means the weight that a bridge, beam or any structure must carry safely.

1.q: Which of these is a real river in India that has a famous bridge over it?
1.e: The Yamuna is a major river in India with famous bridges in Delhi, like the Nizamuddin Bridge.

1.q: What do you call the road surface on top of a bridge that cars drive on?
1.e: The deck is the flat surface on top of the bridge structure that traffic uses.

1.q: Why do bridges have railings on the side?
o: So people and cars do not fall off the edge
1.e: Railings are safety barriers along the sides of a bridge to stop people and vehicles from falling.

1.q: Concrete is a mix of cement, sand, gravel and ___. What fills the blank?
1.e: Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand, gravel and water. It becomes very hard when it dries.

1.q: How many legs does a typical simple bridge have touching the ground or river bed?
1.e: Most simple bridges rest on two supports, one at each end, called abutments or piers.

1.q: What is the name of the famous long sea bridge near Mumbai?
1.e: The Bandra-Worli Sea Link is a cable-stayed bridge across the sea in Mumbai, opened in 2009.

1.q: Which famous bridge in Kolkata uses two tall towers and diagonal cables?
1.e: Vidyasagar Setu is a cable-stayed bridge over the Hooghly river in Kolkata, with two tall pylons.

1.q: What does an engineer do before building a bridge?
1.e: Before building, engineers make detailed plans and drawings so the bridge will be safe and strong.

1.q: What does it mean when engineers say a bridge is 'under tension'?
o: Some parts are being pulled or stretched
1.e: Tension means a pulling force. Cables in a cable bridge are under tension — they are being stretched tight.

1.q: What does 'compression' mean in a bridge?
o: Parts being pushed or squeezed together
1.e: Compression is a pushing force. The pillars (piers) of a bridge are under compression — they are being squashed by the weight above.

1.q: Which material has been used to build bridges for thousands of years and comes from nature?
1.e: Stone bridges have existed for thousands of years. Ancient Romans built many stone arch bridges.

1.q: A bridge 'arch' is curved like a rainbow. What does the arch do?
o: It spreads the weight outward to the sides
1.e: An arch transfers the weight of the bridge outward and downward to the supports on each side.

1.q: If a bridge is 40 metres long and you have already built 15 metres, how many more metres do you need to build?
1.e: 40 - 15 = 25 metres left to build.

1.q: A bridge has 3 lanes for cars. If 2 more lanes are added, how many lanes will it have?
1.e: 3 + 2 = 5 lanes.

1.q: Why do engineers test a model of a bridge before building the real one?
o: To check if the design is safe and will work
1.e: Scale models let engineers spot problems and test ideas before spending money on the real bridge.

1.q: What do you call the part of a bridge that goes deep into the ground or river to hold the bridge up?
1.e: The foundation (or piles) goes deep into the ground or riverbed to carry all the weight of the bridge.

1.q: A cable bridge has 4 big cables. Each cable holds 20 trucks worth of weight. How many trucks can all 4 cables hold?
1.e: 4 × 20 = 80 trucks worth of weight.

1.q: What material do builders pour into a mold that hardens like rock?
1.e: Concrete is poured as a liquid mixture into molds (called formwork) and then sets hard like rock.

1.q: What is the top part of an arch called, right at the highest point?
1.e: The keystone is the wedge-shaped stone at the very top (crown) of an arch. It locks all the other stones in place.

1.q: In a truss bridge, which shape do the steel bars make?
1.e: A truss is a framework of steel bars arranged in triangles. Triangles are stiff and do not bend under load.

1.q: If a bridge weighs 500 tonnes and the river can only hold 400 tonnes, what should the engineer do?
o: Re-design the bridge to be lighter or stronger
1.e: An engineer must always make sure the structure matches what the ground or river can safely hold.

1.q: What does the word 'span' mean for a bridge?
o: The distance the bridge crosses from one side to the other
1.e: The span is the length of the bridge between its supports. A long span means a big gap is crossed.

1.q: What do we call a bridge that hangs from cables attached to tall towers?
1.e: In a suspension bridge, the deck hangs from cables that run over tall towers and are anchored to the ground.

1.q: A builder places 8 steel beams, then 5 more. How many beams are there in total?
1.e: 8 + 5 = 13 beams.

1.q: What is the Golden Gate Bridge famous for?
o: It is the oldest bridge in the world
It is a very long, tall suspension bridge in the United States
1.e: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco, USA is a famous long suspension bridge, opened in 1937.

1.q: Which animal digs burrows that could make the ground under a bridge weak?
1.e: Animals like moles that burrow underground can weaken the soil below a foundation.

1.q: When engineers inspect a bridge, what are they looking for?
1.e: Bridge inspections check for cracks in concrete, rust on steel, and any damage that might make the bridge unsafe.

1.q: What do traffic lights on a bridge help with?
o: They tell drivers when to stop and go safely
1.e: Traffic lights control the flow of vehicles on a bridge, preventing accidents.

1.q: A bridge connects a village with 30 people on one side to a market with 50 people on the other. How many people can now reach the market?
1.e: The 30 people from the village can now cross to the market. (The 50 market people were already there.)

1.q: What do engineers wear on a building site to protect their head?
1.e: Engineers and construction workers wear a hard hat to protect their head from falling objects.

1.q: If a bridge has 6 lanes and each lane is 4 metres wide, how wide is the bridge?
1.e: 6 × 4 = 24 metres wide.

1.q: Rust on steel happens when steel reacts with water and ___. What fills the blank?
1.e: Steel rusts when iron reacts with water and oxygen. Engineers protect steel with paint or special coatings.

1.q: What is the Howrah Bridge famous for?
o: It is a large cantilever bridge over the Hooghly River in Kolkata
1.e: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu) is a massive cantilever truss bridge in Kolkata, opened in 1943.

1.q: What happens to iron and steel if you do not protect them from water?
1.e: Without protection, water and oxygen make iron and steel rust, which slowly weakens the metal.

1.q: If a truck is too heavy for a bridge, what should the driver do?
1.e: Bridges have weight limits (load limits). If a vehicle is too heavy, the driver must find another route.

1.q: A bridge builder uses 10 tonnes of cement today and 8 tonnes tomorrow. How many tonnes in total?
1.e: 10 + 8 = 18 tonnes of cement.

1.q: What does a civil engineer build? (Choose the best answer)
o: Roads, bridges, dams, buildings and tunnels
1.e: Civil engineers design and build infrastructure: roads, bridges, dams, buildings, and tunnels.

1.q: What is the purpose of a dam?
o: To hold back water to create a lake and provide water or electricity
1.e: Dams hold back river water, creating reservoirs for drinking water, irrigation and hydroelectric power.

1.q: What is the longest bridge in India (as of 2024)?
1.e: The Bogibeel Bridge over the Brahmaputra River in Assam is the longest rail-road bridge in India, about 4.9 km.

1.q: Which engineering tool is used to draw straight lines and right angles?
1.e: Engineers use set squares, rulers, compasses and protractors to draw accurate technical plans.

1.q: What does a suspension cable need to be to hold a heavy bridge deck?
1.e: Suspension cables must be made of many steel wires twisted together so they are very strong and do not stretch too much.

1.q: What is a 'blueprint'?
o: A detailed plan or drawing of a structure
1.e: A blueprint is a detailed technical drawing that shows the exact measurements and design of a structure.

1.q: If a team of 5 builders each lay 6 bricks every minute, how many bricks do they lay together in 1 minute?
1.e: 5 × 6 = 30 bricks per minute.

1.q: Why is it important for a bridge to be level (flat) from one side to the other?
o: So it looks nice in photos
So vehicles can drive smoothly and safely
1.e: A level surface lets vehicles travel safely without tipping or skidding.

1.q: In construction, what does PPE stand for?
1.e: PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) includes hard hats, high-visibility vests, gloves and safety boots worn on a building site.

1.q: What is the role of a surveyor before a bridge is built?
o: To measure the land, depth of the river and exact positions
1.e: A surveyor measures the land very accurately — heights, distances, river depth — so the bridge is in the right place.

1.q: A truss bridge has 12 triangles. A second bridge has 8 triangles. How many triangles do both bridges have together?
1.e: 12 + 8 = 20 triangles.

1.q: What safety sign do you see on a construction site that means danger?
o: A yellow triangle with an exclamation mark
1.e: A yellow triangle with an exclamation mark (!) is a universal warning sign meaning 'danger, be careful'.

1.q: Why do engineers put expansion joints in a bridge?
o: To allow the bridge to expand in heat and shrink in cold without cracking
1.e: Metal and concrete expand when hot and shrink when cold. Expansion joints are small gaps that let this movement happen safely.

1.q: What do you call a small bridge that takes a road over a stream or ditch?
1.e: A culvert is a small bridge or pipe structure that carries a road over a small stream or drainage ditch.

1.q: What does 'maintenance' of a bridge mean?
o: Looking after and repairing the bridge regularly so it stays safe
Painting it a new colour every day
1.e: Regular maintenance — painting, fixing cracks, tightening bolts — keeps a bridge safe for many years.

1.q: What is a 'girder' in a bridge?
o: A large, strong horizontal beam that supports the deck
1.e: A girder is a large horizontal beam — made of steel or concrete — that carries the load of the bridge deck.

1.q: If 3 cranes work on a bridge and each lifts 4 steel beams a day, how many beams are lifted in one day?
1.e: 3 × 4 = 12 beams per day.

1.q: If one road joint has no cable, the road there will:
1.e: Every road joint in the middle needs something holding it up.

1.q: Which is stronger for a bridge cable?
1.e: Steel can pull very hard without breaking.

1.q: Which key makes a gap between two words?
1.e: The long space bar puts a space between words.

1.q: Which key takes the cursor to a new line?
1.e: Pressing Enter starts a new line.

1.q: Which key rubs out the letter to the left of the cursor?
1.e: Backspace deletes the character before the cursor.

1.q: We talk into a computer using a:
1.e: A microphone is an input device for sound.

1.q: Which of these is NOT a computer?
1.e: A bicycle is a vehicle, not a computer.

1.q: Clicking the left mouse button two times quickly is called:
1.e: A double-click opens files and programs.

1.q: The small arrow that moves on the screen with the mouse is the:
1.e: The mouse pointer shows where you will click.

1.q: A robot starts at (0, 0). It moves one square each: down, left, down, right. Where does it stop? (right adds 1 to x, up adds 1 to y)
1.e: Count right minus left for x = 0, and up minus down for y = -2.

1.q: A robot starts at (0, 0). It moves one square each: right, up, left, right. Where does it stop? (right adds 1 to x, up adds 1 to y)
1.e: Count right minus left for x = 1, and up minus down for y = 1.

1.q: How many key presses are needed to type 'printer'?
1.e: One press per letter (7) = 7.

1.q: How many key presses are needed to type 'keyboard'?
1.e: One press per letter (8) = 8.

1.q: Money we keep aside for later is called:
1.e: Saving means not spending all money now.

1.q: Indian money is called the:
1.e: India's currency is the Indian Rupee (₹).

1.q: A farmer who grows rice and sells it is a:
1.e: Producers make or grow goods; consumers use them.

1.q: When we buy and use things, we are:
1.e: A consumer buys goods and services to use.

1.q: An animal that has black and white stripes:
1.e: An animal that has black and white stripes — zebra.

1.q: An animal that sleeps through winter (hibernates):
1.e: An animal that sleeps through winter (hibernates) — bear.

1.q: The bird known for its beautiful dance and colourful feathers:
1.e: The bird known for its beautiful dance and colourful feathers — peacock.

1.q: The bird that cannot fly but runs very fast:
1.e: The bird that cannot fly but runs very fast — ostrich.

1.q: Which animal lives in a mound?
1.e: termite — mound.

1.q: Where does a monkey live?
1.e: monkey — tree.

1.q: Which animal lives in a hive?
1.e: honeybee — hive.

1.q: Where does a horse live?
1.e: horse — stable.

1.q: Where does a bird live?
1.e: bird — nest.

1.q: Which animal lives in a eyrie?
1.e: eagle — eyrie.

1.q: Which animal lives in a den?
1.e: lion — den.

1.q: Which animal lives in a sty?
1.e: pig — sty.

1.q: Which animal lives in a web?
1.e: spider — web.

1.q: Where does a hen live?
1.e: hen — coop.

1.q: Where does a squirrel live?
1.e: squirrel — drey.

1.q: Where does a cow live?
1.e: cow — shed.

1.q: Which animal lives in a nest?
1.e: bird — nest.

1.q: Where does a pig live?
1.e: pig — sty.

1.q: Which animal lives in a tree?
1.e: monkey — tree.

1.q: How many legs does a/an housefly have?
1.e: A/an housefly has 6 legs.

1.q: How many legs does a/an spider have?
1.e: A/an spider has 8 legs.

1.q: How many legs does a/an ant have?
1.e: A/an ant has 6 legs.

1.q: How many legs does a/an scorpion have?
1.e: A/an scorpion has 8 legs.

1.q: On a farm there are 9 hens and 7 ducks. How many legs are there in all?
How many legs does a/an earthworm have?
1.e: A/an earthworm has 0 legs.

1.q: On a farm there are 7 geese and 2 horses. How many legs are there in all?
On a farm there are 2 hens and 4 cows. How many legs are there in all?
How many legs does a/an butterfly have?
1.e: A/an butterfly has 6 legs.

1.q: On a farm there are 7 ducks and 3 buffaloes. How many legs are there in all?
On a farm there are 7 sheep and 4 pigs. How many legs are there in all?
How many legs does a/an parrot have?
1.e: A/an parrot has 2 legs.

1.q: On a farm there are 4 sheep and 9 pigs. How many legs are there in all?
On a farm there are 5 dogs and 3 cows. How many legs are there in all?
On a farm there are 8 geese and 7 goats. How many legs are there in all?
Complete the sentence: A sparrow ____.
1.e: sparrow — chirps.

1.q: Complete the sentence: A elephant ____.
1.e: elephant — trumpets.

1.q: Which animal mews?
1.e: cat — mews.

1.q: Which animal brays?
1.e: donkey — brays.

1.q: A very high landform with a peak:
1.e: A very high landform with a peak — mountain.

1.q: In which season are raincoats and umbrellas are used?
1.e: raincoats and umbrellas are used — rainy season.

1.q: Fishing boats are found near the:
1.e: Fishing boats are found near the — sea or river.

1.q: Ice that never melts is found near the:
1.e: Ice that never melts is found near the — North and South Poles.

1.q: Most of the Earth is covered with:
1.e: Most of the Earth is covered with — water.

1.q: Tall trees growing close together make a:
1.e: Tall trees growing close together make a — forest.

1.q: Clouds are made of tiny drops of:
1.e: Clouds are made of tiny drops of — water.

1.q: A small stream of water flowing down a hill:
1.e: A small stream of water flowing down a hill — stream (brook).

1.q: At night we can see the:
1.e: At night we can see the — Moon and stars.

1.q: A big ball-shaped model of the Earth:

1.q: A place with very little rain and lots of sand:
1.e: A place with very little rain and lots of sand — desert.

1.q: Rivers flow into the:
1.e: Rivers flow into the — sea.

1.q: Land that is flat and good for farming:
1.e: Land that is flat and good for farming — plain.

1.e: Order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

1.q: Which planet comes just after Mercury (moving away from the Sun)?
1.e: Order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

1.q: Which planet is number 3 from the Sun?
1.e: Order: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

1.q: What is the position of Uranus from the Sun?

1.q: What is the position of Mars from the Sun?

1.q: What is the position of Neptune from the Sun?

1.q: What is the position of Earth from the Sun?

1.q: What is the position of Mercury from the Sun?

1.q: On a sunny day we may wear:

1.q: The bright arch of colours after rain is a:

1.q: On a snowy day we wear:
1.e: On a snowy day we wear — warm woollen clothes.

1.q: On a rainy day we carry:
1.e: On a rainy day we carry — an umbrella or raincoat.

1.q: Which day comes after Wednesday?

1.q: Which day comes after Monday?
1.e: The days of the week go in order.

1.q: Which day comes after Sunday?
1.e: The days of the week go in order.

1.q: Which day comes before Thursday?
1.e: The days of the week go in order.

1.e: The months go in order.

1.e: The months go in order.

1.q: Which month comes after July?

1.q: Which month comes after December?
1.e: The months go in order.

1.e: A triangle has 3 corners.

1.q: How many corners (vertices) does a octagon have?

1.q: How many sides does a octagon have?
1.e: A octagon has 8 sides.

1.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?

1.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
1.e: A pentagon has 5 sides.

Which bridge shape pushes its weight outwards into the river banks, like a curved rainbow?
1.e: An arch turns the weight into a push along its curve and down into strong ground at each end. Romans built arches 2000 years ago!

1.q: In a suspension bridge, the road hangs from...
1.e: Huge cables run over tall towers, and smaller cables hang down to hold the road.

1.q: What simple machine is a see-saw?
1.e: A lever is a bar that turns around a point called the pivot (fulcrum).

1.q: A pulley helps you...
o: Lift heavy things by pulling down on a rope
1.e: A rope over a wheel lets you pull down to lift up - easier, because you can use your weight.

1.q: You use a long stick to lift a heavy rock. Where should the small stone (pivot) go?
1.e: Pivot near the load and push far away: a small push lifts a big weight. That is leverage!

1.q: Which is a wheel and axle?
1.e: Turning the big knob turns the small rod inside - a wheel and axle makes turning easier.

1.q: A ramp is also called...
1.e: An inclined plane is a slope. Pushing a load up a long slope needs less force than lifting it straight up.

1.q: Which ramp needs the smallest push to get a cart to the top?
1.e: A gentle ramp is longer but needs less push at every step - the same trick mountain roads use.

1.q: A screw is really an inclined plane wrapped around...
1.e: The spiral thread on a screw is a ramp wound round a rod, so turning it drives it in with great force.

1.q: An axe splits wood easily because its edge is a...
1.e: A wedge is a thin edge that pushes things apart. Knives and teeth are wedges too!

1.q: A thick plank and a thin plank of the same wood span a stream. Which bends less?
1.e: Thicker beams are much stiffer. Doubling the thickness makes a plank about 8 times stiffer!

1.q: A plank lying flat or standing on its edge - which way is stiffer for a bridge?
1.e: Standing on edge makes it deep. Depth fights bending far better than width - that is why beams are tall.

1.q: What does a spring do when you squash it and let go?
1.e: Springs store the push and give it back. Car suspensions use springs for a smooth ride.

1.q: Which pushes harder on the floor: you standing on one foot or on two?
o: The same total weight - but one foot presses harder per spot
1.e: Your weight is the same either way. On one foot it is squeezed onto a smaller area, so the pressure is bigger.

1.q: Why do camels and snowshoes have big flat feet?
o: To spread weight and not sink
1.e: Big feet spread the weight over more area, so they do not sink into sand or snow. Bridge pillars stand on wide footings for the same reason.

1.q: A big drum and a small drum: which makes the lower, deeper sound?
1.e: Bigger things vibrate more slowly, giving a lower pitch.

1.q: A tight guitar string and a loose one: which gives the higher note?
1.e: Tighter strings vibrate faster, making a higher pitch.

1.q: What is an echo?
o: A sound bouncing back from a wall or hill
1.e: Shout towards a cliff and the sound reflects back to you a moment later.

1.q: When is your shadow the longest?
1.e: When the sun is low in the sky, shadows stretch out long. At noon the sun is high and shadows are short.

1.q: A mirror shows your right hand as...
1.e: A mirror flips left and right, so your raised right hand looks like a left hand in the reflection.

1.q: Which material lets only some light through (frosted glass, tissue paper)?
1.e: Transparent: all light through. Translucent: some light, blurry view. Opaque: no light.

1.q: Why do we see a rainbow after rain?
o: Sunlight is split into colours by water drops
1.e: White sunlight is a mix of colours. Raindrops bend each colour a different amount and spread them out.

1.q: How many colours do we usually name in a rainbow?
1.e: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet - 7 colours.

1.q: Which keeps a cup of tea hot longer?
o: A cup with a lid in a woollen cover
A cup by an open window
1.e: Lids and wool stop heat escaping. Materials that slow heat are called insulators.

1.q: Which travels fastest?
1.e: Light is the fastest thing there is - about 300,000 kilometres every second!

1.q: A heavy box is easier to slide on rollers (round logs). Why?
o: Rolling has much less friction than sliding
1.e: Ancient builders moved giant stones on log rollers. Rolling beats dragging!

1.q: A heavy cart and a light cart are pushed with the same force. Which speeds up faster?
1.e: The same push makes a lighter thing speed up more. Heavy things need bigger pushes.

1.q: Why is it hard to stop a heavy train quickly?
o: It carries a lot of moving 'oomph' (momentum)
1.e: Momentum is mass times speed. A heavy, fast train has huge momentum and needs a long distance to stop.

1.q: Iron filings near a magnet line up in a pattern. What does the pattern show?
1.e: The filings follow the magnetic field lines that spread from one pole to the other.

1.q: A compass needle always points...
1.e: A compass needle is a tiny magnet that lines up with the Earth's magnetic field.

1.q: Why do skyscrapers and tall bridges sway a little in strong wind?
o: They are built to bend slightly instead of snapping
1.e: A tiny sway is safe and planned. Being a little flexible stops tall structures from cracking.

1.q: A ball is dropped from a high window and a low window. Which hits the ground faster?
1.e: The longer it falls, the more time gravity has to speed it up.

1.q: Which is a good way to make a paper tower stronger?
1.e: Tubes are hard to bend and buckle. Steel towers are often hollow tubes for the same reason.

1.q: When you jump on a trampoline, why do you bounce up?
o: The springy mat stretches and pushes you back
1.e: Your weight stretches the mat; the stretched mat pushes back and throws you up.

1.q: A rope pulled tight between two posts can hold up a hanging lamp. The rope is in...
1.e: Ropes and cables only work when pulled tight - that is tension.

1.q: A pillar holding up a roof is being...
1.e: The roof's weight pushes down on the pillar and the ground pushes up: the pillar is squeezed.

1.q: What happens to a long thin stick if you squeeze its ends together hard?
1.e: Long thin things squeezed at the ends bow out sideways. Engineers call this buckling.

1.q: Which is the shortest stick and so the hardest to buckle?
1.e: Short and thick sticks resist buckling far better than long thin ones.

1.q: Where is it easier to pedal a bicycle?
1.e: On the flat you do not fight gravity, and the hard road has little rolling resistance.

1.q: What does a seat belt do in a car that suddenly stops?
o: Holds you so you do not keep moving forward
1.e: Your body wants to keep moving when the car stops. The belt stops you safely.

1.q: A heavy door with the handle near the hinge would be...
1.e: Turning effect = force x distance from the hinge. A handle near the hinge gives little turning effect.

1.q: Which is a source of sound?
1.e: A bell vibrates when struck, making sound waves.

1.q: Why do we hear a train coming before we see it around a bend?
o: Sound travels around corners and through the ground
1.e: Sound spreads around obstacles and even travels along the rails. Light goes in straight lines.

1.q: Which is the best insulator to keep ice from melting in a lunch box?
o: A wet cloth in the sun
1.e: Foam is full of trapped air, which slows heat from getting in.

1.q: A toy boat is pushed by wind on its sail. Which way does it go?
1.e: The wind pushes the sail, so the boat moves along with the wind.

1.q: Why do tall bridge towers often get thicker at the bottom?
o: Wind blows only at the top
The bottom carries the weight of everything above
1.e: Each part of a tower holds up everything above it, so the bottom carries the most.

1.q: You push a swing gently many times at the right moment. The swing goes...
1.e: Small pushes in time with the swing add up. This is resonance - great for swings, dangerous for bridges in wind!

1.q: Soldiers marching in step are told to break step on a bridge. Why?
o: Marching in step can shake the bridge in rhythm
1.e: Many feet stamping in rhythm could match the bridge's natural swing and build up big wobbles.

1.q: What makes a hot-air balloon rise?
o: Hot air inside is lighter than the cooler air outside
1.e: Heating air makes it spread out and become lighter, so the balloon floats up.

1.q: Two equal weights hang on a balance, one on each side, at the same distance. The balance...
1.e: Equal weights at equal distances balance exactly.

1.q: Which object has the most friction when you slide it on the floor?
1.e: Rubber grips the floor strongly. Ice is slippery; trays and marbles slide or roll easily.

1.q: Why do we oil a squeaky door hinge?
o: Oil reduces friction so it moves smoothly and quietly
1.e: Oil makes surfaces slippery, cutting friction - and the squeak.

1.q: A car's brakes get hot after a long downhill drive. Why?
o: Friction turns the car's motion into heat
1.e: Brakes rub to slow the car, turning moving energy into heat. Long hills make lots of heat.

1.q: Which wheel would roll farthest after one push on a smooth floor?
o: A wheel with a flat side
1.e: A smooth round wheel loses little energy to bumps and friction, so it rolls far.

1.q: A clock pendulum swings back and forth. A longer pendulum swings...
1.e: Longer pendulums take more time for each swing. Bridges also have a 'swing time' that depends on their size and stiffness.

1.q: Which helps a heavy truck stop on a wet road?
1.e: Wet roads have less grip, so stopping takes longer. Slow down and brake earlier.

1.q: Which bridge would be best to cross a very long, wide river?
o: A suspension bridge with tall towers and cables
1.e: Suspension bridges can span the longest gaps - over 1 kilometre between towers!

1.q: A beam bridge is simply...
o: A straight beam resting on supports at each end
1.e: The simplest bridge: a beam across a gap, like a log over a stream.

1.q: A truss bridge is strong because it is made of...
1.e: Triangles cannot change shape, so a truss of triangles is strong and light - like the bridges you build in MODIS BridgeWorks.

1.q: Why do we see lightning as a straight-ish bright line from far away?
o: Light travels in straight lines to our eyes
1.e: Light from the flash travels straight to us, so we see where it happened instantly.

1.q: You count 3 seconds between lightning and thunder. Is the storm near or far?
1.e: Sound travels about 1 kilometre in 3 seconds. Count the seconds to measure the distance!

1.q: A kite string is pulled tight by the wind. If the string breaks, the kite...
o: Is blown away by the wind
1.e: The string held the kite against the wind. Without it, the wind carries the kite away.

1.q: Which is the right unit to measure the length of a bridge?
1.e: Length is measured in metres (or kilometres for very long bridges).

1.q: Which unit measures how heavy a truck is?
1.e: 1 tonne = 1000 kilograms. Bridge signs show weight limits in tonnes.

1.q: A thick wall of snow keeps an igloo warm inside. Why?
o: Igloos have heaters inside the walls
Snow is full of trapped air, a good insulator
1.e: Packed snow traps air, which slows heat escaping - surprising but true!

1.q: What is 'gravity' pulling you towards when you stand on the ground?
1.e: Earth's gravity pulls everything towards its centre - that is 'down' everywhere on the planet.

1.q: Astronauts on the Moon can jump very high. Why?
o: The Moon's gravity is much weaker than Earth's
They have springs in their shoes
There is wind on the Moon
1.e: The Moon pulls about 6 times less than the Earth, so a jump goes much higher.

1.q: A loaded truck makes a wooden bridge sag in the middle. What would reduce the sag?
o: Add a support (pillar) in the middle
1.e: A middle support halves the span, and shorter spans bend far less.

1.q: Which simple machine helps lift a car to change a tyre?
1.e: A car jack uses a screw or lever so a small push lifts a heavy car slowly.

1.q: Why does a basketball bounce higher than a ball of clay?
o: The basketball is springy and gives back the energy
1.e: The basketball squashes and springs back. Clay squashes and stays squashed, keeping the energy as heat.

1.q: Which sound is higher pitched?
1.e: Small fast vibrations make high sounds, like a bird's tweet.

1.q: Water in a hose shoots out further when you squeeze the end. Why?
o: The same water must rush out through a smaller hole, faster
1.e: A smaller opening makes the water speed up - a lesson in pressure and flow.

1.q: The water at the bottom of a deep tank pushes harder than at the top. Why?
o: All the water above presses down on it
1.e: Deeper water carries the weight of all the water above. That is why dams are thicker at the bottom.

1.q: Which travels through space from the Sun to Earth?
1.e: Light and heat cross empty space. Sound needs air or something to travel through.

1.q: A swing hangs from two chains. Each chain is...
1.e: The seat's weight pulls on the chains - like hangers on a suspension bridge.

1.q: What helps a sailing ship move without an engine?
1.e: Sails catch the wind's push. For centuries, ships crossed oceans this way.

1.q: Why is a bridge deck often made slightly curved upwards in the middle?
o: So it does not look or become saggy when loaded
1.e: Builders add a small upward curve (camber) so that under weight the deck ends up nearly flat - and rain runs off.

1.q: Which is a non-contact force (it works without touching)?
1.e: Magnets pull iron from a distance. Gravity is another non-contact force.

1.q: Two magnets pull together when...
o: Opposite poles (north and south) face each other
The same poles face each other
1.e: North pulls south. North pushes north, and south pushes south.

1.q: Why do roads have gentle curves instead of sharp corners on fast highways?
o: Fast cars need gentle turns to stay on the road
To make roads longer for fun
1.e: Turning sharply at high speed needs a huge sideways grip. Gentle curves keep cars safe.

1.q: A heavier bucket on a pulley needs...
o: A bigger pull on the rope
1.e: A heavier load needs more force. Using two pulleys can share the load and halve the pull.

1.q: What is the job of a bridge's foundation?
o: To pass the bridge's weight safely into the ground
1.e: Foundations spread the huge weight of a bridge into firm ground or rock so it does not sink.

1.q: Which is the best way to keep a tent from blowing away?
o: Tie it to pegs with tight ropes
1.e: Tight guy ropes pull the tent down and sideways against the wind - the same idea as bridge stay cables.

1.q: You blow over the top of a strip of paper. The paper...
1.e: Fast-moving air over the paper has lower pressure, so the paper lifts - like a plane's wing.

1.q: A hammer pulls out a nail using its claw. The hammer is acting as a...
1.e: The hammer turns about its head on the wood: a small pull on the long handle gives a big pull on the nail.

1.q: Why do cyclists bend low on fast downhill rides?
o: To look at the road better
1.e: Bending low makes a smaller shape, so the air pushes back less (less drag).

1.q: Which bridge would likely sway most in a strong wind?
1.e: Long, light and narrow structures are easier for the wind to shake. Engineers add stiffness or dampers.

1.q: What happens to the height of a ball's bounce each time it bounces?
o: It stays exactly the same forever
1.e: Each bounce loses a little energy to heat and sound, so the ball bounces lower and lower.

1.q: Which is a contact force?
1.e: Friction only works where two surfaces touch.

1.q: You rub a balloon on your hair and it sticks to the wall. What caused this?
1.e: Rubbing moves tiny charges onto the balloon, and charged things can stick to walls.

1.q: A roller coaster car speeds up going down a slope and slows going up. Why?
o: Gravity speeds it downhill and slows it uphill
1.e: Going down, height turns into speed; going up, speed turns back into height.

1.q: Why are tyres filled with air?
o: Air is springy and cushions bumps
1.e: Squashed air pushes back like a spring, giving a smoother ride and gripping the road.

1.q: A crane lifts steel beams to the top of a bridge. Which simple machines does it use?
1.e: Cranes use pulleys (ropes over wheels) and long arms (levers) to lift huge weights.

1.q: Which is NOT a simple machine?
1.e: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge and screw.

1.q: A bridge in a cold country has a small gap where it meets the road. What is it for?
o: To let the bridge grow and shrink with heat and cold
To let rain fall through for fun
1.e: Bridges expand on hot days and shrink on cold days. Expansion joints give them room.

1.q: If you push a toy car twice as hard, it usually goes...
1.e: A bigger force gives a bigger speed-up.

1.q: Why does a stone sink but a large log float?
o: The log is lighter for its size than water
1.e: What matters is how heavy something is for its size (density). Wood is less dense than water; stone is denser.

1.q: Which is the best tool to find which of two parcels is heavier?
1.e: A balance tips towards the heavier side.

1.q: A thermometer measures...
o: How hot or cold something is
1.e: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius with a thermometer.

1.q: Why do builders use cranes instead of carrying steel by hand?
o: Machines multiply force so huge loads can be lifted
Steel is too light to carry
1.e: Simple machines trade a long pull for a big lift - no one can lift a 10-tonne beam by hand!

1.q: What are the three main states of matter?
1.e: Everything is a solid (keeps its shape), a liquid (flows) or a gas (spreads everywhere).

1.q: What do we call it when a liquid turns into a gas?
1.e: Puddles drying in the sun is evaporation: water becomes water vapour.

1.q: What do we call it when a gas turns back into a liquid?
1.e: Steam hitting a cold mirror turns back into water drops - condensation.

1.q: What do we call it when a solid turns into a liquid?
1.e: Ice melting into water, butter melting in a pan - solid to liquid.

1.q: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?
1.e: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and freezes at 0 degrees Celsius.

1.q: Why does a liquid take the shape of its container?
o: Its particles can slide past each other
1.e: In a liquid the tiny particles are close but free to move, so it flows to fill the bottom of any container.

1.q: Why does a solid keep its shape?
o: Its particles are held tightly in place
1.e: In a solid the particles are locked together, so it keeps its own shape.

1.q: Why does a smell spread through a whole room?
1.e: Gases spread to fill all the space they can. That is why you smell cooking from the next room.

1.q: You leave a glass of water out for a week. The water level goes down. Why?
o: Someone drank it secretly every night
1.e: Even without boiling, water slowly evaporates at room temperature.

1.q: How can you get salt back from salty water?
1.e: When the water evaporates, the salt is left behind as crystals - that is how sea salt is made.

1.q: Muddy water is poured through a filter paper. What comes through?
1.e: The filter traps the solid bits of mud and lets the water pass.

1.q: Which can be separated with a magnet?
1.e: A magnet pulls the iron out and leaves the sand behind.

1.q: What is a solution?
o: A mixture where one thing dissolves in another
1.e: Salt water and sugar water are solutions: the solid has dissolved and you cannot see it.

1.q: What makes sugar dissolve faster in water?
1.e: Stirring and warmth help the water break the sugar apart faster.

1.q: Steel is mostly made from which metal?
1.e: Steel is iron with a little carbon added, which makes it much stronger.

1.q: Why is steel used for bridges instead of pure iron?
1.e: Adding carbon to iron makes steel - strong in pulling and pushing, and tough enough not to shatter.

1.q: What do we call a metal made by mixing metals together, like steel or brass?
1.e: Alloys combine metals (or a metal and carbon) to get better properties.

1.q: Which material does NOT rust?
1.e: Only iron and steel rust. Plastic never rusts.

1.q: What two things does iron need to rust?
1.e: Rust forms when iron meets both water and oxygen. Keep either away and rust slows down.

1.q: Which coating protects steel from rust?
o: Paint or a layer of zinc
1.e: Paint keeps water out. A zinc coating (galvanising) even protects scratched spots.

1.q: What is concrete mainly good at?
1.e: Concrete is very strong when pushed but cracks when pulled. That is why steel bars are put inside it.

1.q: Why are steel bars (rebar) put inside concrete?
o: Steel takes the pulling forces concrete cannot
1.e: Reinforced concrete: concrete handles squeezing, steel handles pulling - a perfect team.

1.q: Wood comes from trees. What is it made of?
1.e: Wood fibres run along the trunk, so wood is strongest along the grain.

1.q: Which material burns easily?
1.e: Wood is a fuel. That is why wooden bridges need protection from fire.

1.q: What is left after wood burns?
1.e: Burning changes wood into ash, smoke and gases - a change that cannot be reversed.

1.q: A fire needs fuel, heat and...
1.e: Take away oxygen (cover it with a blanket or sand) and a fire goes out.

1.q: Which is a reversible change?
1.e: Melted chocolate sets again when it cools. Burning and cooking cannot be undone.

1.q: Which is an irreversible change?
1.e: Rust is a new substance; it does not turn back into shiny iron by itself.

1.q: Why do we keep cooking oil away from the stove flame?
1.e: Hot oil is flammable. Never pour water on an oil fire - cover it instead.

1.q: Glass is made from melting...
1.e: Sand melted at about 1500 °C and cooled becomes glass.

1.q: Plastic is mostly made from...
1.e: Most plastics are made from chemicals in crude oil.

1.q: Why is plastic litter a problem in rivers and seas?
o: It takes hundreds of years to break down and harms animals
1.e: Plastic lasts a very long time and animals can swallow it or get tangled.

1.q: What happens to clay when it is fired in a kiln?
o: It becomes hard pottery or brick
1.e: High heat changes clay permanently into hard ceramic.

1.q: Which is the hardest natural material?
1.e: Diamond is so hard it is used on saw blades to cut stone and concrete.

1.q: Mortar between bricks is made of cement, sand and...
1.e: Water starts the chemical reaction that makes cement harden.

1.q: Why do builders add gravel (small stones) to concrete instead of using only cement?
o: Stones add strength and stop too much shrinking and cracking
1.e: Pure cement paste shrinks and cracks like dry mud. Stones and sand give bulk and strength.

1.q: A shiny metal spoon left in salty water for weeks may...
1.e: Salty water speeds up corrosion of many metals.

1.q: Which property makes copper good for electric wires?
1.e: Copper lets electricity flow easily and can be pulled into thin wires.

1.q: Why are pan handles often plastic or wood?
o: They are insulators - they do not get hot quickly
1.e: Insulators slow heat flow, so you can hold the handle safely.

1.q: What do we call materials that let heat move through them easily?
1.e: Metals are good heat conductors.

1.q: Why does a metal railing feel colder than a wooden bench on a cold morning?
o: Metal carries heat away from your hand faster
1.e: Both are the same temperature, but metal conducts heat away from your hand much faster.

1.q: What happens to most materials when they get hot?
1.e: Heat makes particles move more and spread out. Bridges and rails have gaps to allow for this.

1.q: A tight jar lid can be loosened by running hot water over it. Why?
o: The metal lid expands more than the glass
1.e: Metal expands more than glass when heated, so the lid loosens.

1.q: What do we call air with a lot of water vapour in it?
1.e: Humid air feels sticky and slows drying. Wood gets weaker when it soaks up moisture.

1.q: Why do wooden bridges get weaker in wet, humid places?
o: Wood soaks up water and softens or rots
1.e: Wet wood loses strength and can rot. In MODIS BridgeWorks, timber keeps only 70% of its strength in humid levels.

1.q: Which of these is a natural fibre?
1.e: Cotton grows on plants. Nylon, polyester and acrylic are made in factories.

1.q: Why do steel bridges near the sea need more care?
o: Salt in the air speeds up rust
1.e: Salt spray makes corrosion faster, so coastal steel needs thicker protection.

1.q: Vinegar and lemon juice taste sour because they are...
1.e: Acids taste sour. Strong acids can also eat away at stone and concrete over time.

1.q: Soap feels slippery because it is a...
1.e: Bases (alkalis) like soap feel slippery. Acids and bases are chemical opposites.

1.q: Why must cement be kept dry until it is used?
1.e: Cement reacts with water and sets. A wet bag turns into a useless rock.

1.q: Which material is best for a bridge cable that must pull with great force?
1.e: Steel wire is extremely strong in tension - perfect for bridge cables.

1.q: What is the main gas in the air we breathe?
1.e: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. We need the oxygen part.

1.q: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?
1.e: Our bodies use oxygen and make carbon dioxide, which we breathe out.

1.q: Party balloons that float up are filled with...
1.e: Helium is lighter than air, so helium balloons float up.

1.q: Fizzy drinks have bubbles of which gas?
1.e: Carbon dioxide is dissolved in the drink under pressure; opening the bottle lets it bubble out.

1.q: Why does a fizzy drink go flat if left open?
o: The gas escapes into the air
1.e: Without the cap, the dissolved carbon dioxide slowly escapes.

1.q: What is 'matter'?
o: Anything that has mass and takes up space
1.e: Rocks, water, air and you are all matter.

1.q: Which has the biggest gaps between its particles?
1.e: Gas particles are far apart and zoom around - that is why gases can be squashed.

1.q: You can squash air in a bicycle pump but not water. Why?
o: Gas particles have space between them; liquid particles are close together
1.e: Liquids are hard to compress because their particles are already touching.

1.q: Which is a mixture you can separate by picking out the parts?
1.e: In nuts and raisins you can see and pick each part. In solutions the parts are hidden.

1.q: Why do pearls of dew form on grass on cool mornings?
o: Water vapour in the air condenses on cold grass
1.e: Cool grass chills the air touching it, and vapour turns into droplets - condensation.

1.q: Rain, clouds, rivers and the sea are all part of the...
1.e: Water evaporates, condenses into clouds, falls as rain and flows back to the sea - over and over.

1.q: Why do roads crack after many hot days and cold nights?
o: Heating and cooling make them expand and shrink again and again
1.e: Repeated expanding and shrinking makes materials tired and cracked over time.

1.q: Water that gets into a crack and freezes can...
o: Widen the crack, because ice takes more space
1.e: Water expands when it freezes and pushes cracks apart. This breaks rocks and damages roads.

1.q: Which material is waterproof and used to cover bridge decks under the road?
1.e: A waterproof layer stops rain soaking into the concrete and rusting the steel inside.

1.q: What is the solid left in a kettle in places with hard water?
1.e: Hard water has dissolved minerals. When it boils away, the chalky minerals are left behind.

1.q: Chalk fizzes in vinegar. What is happening?
o: An acid is reacting and making a gas
1.e: Acid reacts with chalk (a carbonate) and gives off carbon dioxide bubbles. Acid rain damages limestone buildings this way.

1.q: Why are old statues sometimes worn away in cities?
o: Acid rain slowly dissolves the stone
1.e: Pollution makes rain slightly acidic, which eats away limestone and marble over the years.

1.q: Which is the best material for a non-stick, heat-proof oven glove?
o: Thick cloth with an insulating layer
1.e: Thick insulating fabric slows heat getting to your hand.

1.q: Which is a sign that a chemical change happened?
o: A new colour, gas bubbles or a smell appear
1.e: New substances often show up as colour changes, fizzing, heat or new smells.

1.q: Why does bread go mouldy if kept too long?
1.e: Mould is a fungus that feeds on old bread, especially in warm, damp places.

1.q: Which is the best way to keep a bridge's steel strong for 100 years?
o: Leave it bare in the rain
Protect it with paint and inspect it regularly
1.e: Coatings plus regular inspection and repainting stop rust before it weakens the steel.

1.q: Wet sand is heavier than dry sand. Why?
o: Water fills the gaps between the grains
1.e: Water sits in the spaces between grains and adds its own weight.

1.q: What is a 'crystal'?
o: A solid with particles in a neat repeating pattern
1.e: Salt, sugar, snowflakes and diamonds are crystals.

1.q: Which material would you choose for a bridge in a very wet jungle?
o: Treated, protected timber or galvanised steel
1.e: In wet places you need materials that resist rot and rust, or that are protected from them.

1.q: What makes an ice cube melt faster?
o: Keeping it in the shade in winter
1.e: More heat from the surroundings melts ice faster. Wool would actually slow melting!

1.q: What is 'oxygen' needed for in burning?
o: The fuel combines with it to release heat
1.e: Burning is a reaction between fuel and oxygen that gives out heat and light.

1.q: Why do builders mix lime or cement with soil to make stronger ground for roads?
o: The chemicals bind the soil grains together
1.e: Stabilised soil is harder and carries heavy trucks without sinking.

1.q: Rubber gloves protect an electrician because rubber is...
1.e: Rubber does not let electricity pass, keeping the electrician safe.

1.q: What is 'evaporation' used for in salt farms by the sea?
o: Letting the sun dry sea water to leave salt
1.e: Shallow pools of sea water are left in the sun; the water evaporates and salt remains.

1.q: Which change happens when you mix flour, water and yeast and wait?
o: The dough rises as gas is made
1.e: Yeast is alive and makes carbon dioxide gas, which puffs up the dough.

1.q: Why do we store petrol in sealed cans away from heat?
o: It evaporates easily and its vapour can catch fire
1.e: Petrol vapour is highly flammable. Sealed cans and cool places keep it safe.

1.q: A cold drink can 'sweats' on a warm day. Is the can leaking?
o: No - water vapour from the air is condensing on it
The drink is evaporating through the metal
1.e: The cold can cools the air around it, and vapour condenses into drops on the outside.

1.q: Why is gold used in jewellery for thousands of years?
o: It does not rust or tarnish and stays shiny
1.e: Gold barely reacts with air or water, so it stays bright for centuries.

1.q: Which word means 'easily catches fire'?
1.e: Flammable materials like paper, wood and petrol burn easily.

1.q: Which material is both strong and light, used in bikes and aeroplanes?
1.e: Aluminium alloys are light and strong and do not rust like iron.

1.q: Steam from a kettle is invisible right at the spout. The white cloud a little further away is...
o: Tiny water droplets after the steam cools
1.e: True steam is invisible gas; as it cools it condenses into tiny visible droplets.

1.q: What do we call it when a solid seems to vanish into a liquid, like salt in soup?
1.e: Dissolving is different from melting: the salt is still there, spread out in the water.

1.q: Why does a puddle dry faster on a windy day?
o: Wind carries away the water vapour
1.e: Moving air removes the damp air above the puddle, so more water can evaporate.

1.q: A sugar cube and powdered sugar are put in water. Which dissolves faster?
1.e: Tiny pieces have more surface touching the water, so they dissolve faster.

1.q: Which property describes how hard it is to scratch a material?
1.e: Hardness tells us how well a material resists scratches and dents.

1.q: Which property describes a material that can be bent without breaking?
1.e: Flexible materials bend. Brittle materials snap.

1.q: Which word describes something that dissolves?
1.e: Sugar and salt are soluble in water; sand and chalk are insoluble.

1.q: Rubbish is sorted into paper, plastic, glass and metal at a recycling centre. Why?
o: Each material is recycled in its own way
1.e: Glass is melted, paper is pulped, metals are melted separately - so they must be sorted first.

1.q: Old steel from a broken bridge can be...
o: Melted and made into new steel
1.e: Steel is one of the most recycled materials - that is part of the 'salvage' you recover in MODIS BridgeWorks!

1.q: Which is the best reason to use recycled steel?
o: It cannot be used for bridges
It saves energy and raw materials
1.e: Recycling steel uses much less energy than making it from iron ore.

1.q: What is iron ore?
o: Rock containing iron that is dug from the ground
1.e: Iron ore is mined and heated in a blast furnace to get iron, which becomes steel.

1.q: A hot steel bar glows red. What happens when it cools?
o: It stops glowing and becomes hard again
1.e: Very hot metal gives off light. As it cools, it goes dark and hardens.

1.q: Which is safest to put out a small fire in a frying pan?
1.e: A lid cuts off oxygen. Water on hot oil can splash and spread the fire.

1.q: A bridge crew lays 23 planks before lunch and 14 after. How many planks?
1.e: 23 + 14 = 37. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: 35 cars cross in the morning and 22 at night. How many cars?
1.e: 35 + 22 = 57. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A school has 41 boys and 37 girls in Class 2. How many children?
1.e: 41 + 37 = 78. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: You read 28 pages on Monday and 15 on Tuesday. How many pages?
1.e: 28 + 15 = 43. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A train carries 46 people in one coach and 29 in another. How many people?
1.e: 46 + 29 = 75. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A shop sells 57 mangoes and 18 oranges. How many fruits?
1.e: 57 + 18 = 75. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A wall has 64 red bricks and 25 grey bricks. How many bricks?
1.e: 64 + 25 = 89. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: Two lorries each carry 19 bags of cement. How many bags?
1.e: 19 + 19 = 38. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A farmer picks 38 kg of rice and then 45 kg more. How many kg?
1.e: 38 + 45 = 83. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: 52 birds sit on a cable and 39 more join. How many birds?
1.e: 52 + 39 = 91. Add the tens, then the ones.

1.q: A bridge needs 65 bolts. 23 are already in. How many still to fit?
You have Rs 80 and spend Rs 35. How much is left?
A road is 94 m long. 41 m is finished. How many metres are left?
A tank holds 72 litres. 28 litres are used. How many litres remain?
50 cones line a bridge. Workers remove 17. How many cones are left?
A crane can lift 86 tonnes. A beam weighs 59 tonnes. How many more tonnes could it lift?
A bridge is 100 m long. A walker has gone 45 m. How far is left?
There were 61 sweets in a jar. 24 were eaten. How many remain?
A train had 43 passengers. 19 got off. How many are on the train now?
A builder had 77 tiles and used 38. How many tiles are left?
3 trucks each carry 5 beams. How many beams?
1.e: 3 groups of 5: 3 x 5 = 15.

1.q: 4 boxes hold 10 nails each. How many nails?
1.e: 4 groups of 10: 4 x 10 = 40.

1.q: A bridge has 6 spans, each 5 m long. How long is the bridge?
1.e: 6 groups of 5: 6 x 5 = 30.

1.q: 8 bags each hold 10 kg of sand. How many kg?
1.e: 8 groups of 10: 8 x 10 = 80.

1.q: 9 coins of Rs 5. How many rupees?
1.e: 9 groups of 5: 9 x 5 = 45.

1.q: A train has 3 wagons with 10 tonnes in each. How many tonnes?
1.e: 3 groups of 10: 3 x 10 = 30.

1.q: A truss has 4 triangles. Each has 3 sides. How many sides if none are shared?
1.e: 4 groups of 3: 4 x 3 = 12.

1.q: 10 buses each carry 10 children. How many children?
7 days of saving Rs 5. How much is saved?
1.e: 7 groups of 5: 7 x 5 = 35.

1.q: 20 sweets shared equally by 5 friends. How many each?
30 bricks packed in stacks of 10. How many stacks?
A 40 m bridge has a lamp every 5 m. How many lamp gaps?
24 wheels are shared among cars with 4 wheels each. How many cars?
Rs 50 paid in Rs 10 notes. How many notes?
16 children make teams of 4. How many teams?
A truck carries 5 tonnes per trip. How many trips for 35 tonnes?
In 47, what is the value of the 4?
1.e: 47 = 4 tens + 7 ones, so the 4 means 40.

1.q: Which number is 6 tens and 3 ones?
1.e: 6 tens = 60, plus 3 = 63.

1.q: Which sign makes this true: 58 __ 85?
1.e: 58 is less than 85, so 58 < 85.

1.q: Round 47 to the nearest ten.
1.e: 47 is closer to 50 than to 40.
Adding 5 each time: 25 + 5 = 30.

1.q: What is one half of 30?
1.e: Halve means split into 2 equal parts: 30 ÷ 2 = 15.

1.q: What is one quarter of 20?
1.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

1.q: What is one third of 12?
1.e: A third is 1 of 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

1.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. You eat 2. What fraction did you eat?
1.e: 2 out of 4 equal slices is 2/4 = 1/2.

1.q: Which shape has 6 square faces?
1.e: A cube (like a dice) has 6 square faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.

1.q: Which 3D shape is a tin of beans?
1.e: A cylinder has two flat circle ends and one curved side - like a tin or a bridge pier.

1.q: Which 3D shape is an ice-cream cone?
1.e: A cone has one circle face and comes to a point.

1.q: How many corners (vertices) does a cube have?
1.e: A cube has 8 corners: 4 on top and 4 underneath.

1.q: A shape is symmetrical if...
o: One half is a mirror image of the other
1.e: Fold it along the line of symmetry and both halves match.

1.q: Many bridges look symmetrical. Why do engineers like that?
o: Loads are shared evenly on both sides
It is a law of colours
1.e: A symmetrical bridge carries weight evenly, so neither side is overloaded.

1.q: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
Which is the best unit to measure the water in a bucket?
1.e: Capacity is measured in litres (l) and millilitres (ml).

1.q: A beam is 3 m long. Another is 250 cm long. Which is longer?
1.e: 3 m = 300 cm, which is more than 250 cm.

1.q: What time is half past 4?
1.e: Half past means 30 minutes after the hour.

1.q: What time is quarter past 7?
1.e: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

1.q: What time is quarter to 9?
1.e: Quarter to 9 is 15 minutes before 9 o'clock.

1.q: A bus leaves at 2:00 and the trip takes 30 minutes. When does it arrive?
How many days are in 2 weeks?
1.e: 1 week = 7 days, so 2 weeks = 14 days.

1.q: A tally shows ||||| ||| . What number is that?
1.e: A full group of 5 plus 3 more = 8.

1.q: In a class vote: bus 12, train 9, bike 5. How many more chose bus than bike?
In the same vote (bus 12, train 9, bike 5), how many children voted?
What is the missing number? 4 x __ = 20
What is the missing number? __ - 15 = 30
1.e: Add back: 30 + 15 = 45.

1.q: Which multiplication matches 5 + 5 + 5 + 5?
1.e: Four groups of five: 4 x 5 = 20.

1.q: Is 3 x 4 the same as 4 x 3?
1.e: Multiplication can be done in any order: 3 x 4 = 4 x 3 = 12.

1.q: Which numbers are all in the 2 times table?
1.e: The 2 times table counts in twos: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10...

1.q: Numbers in the 10 times table always end in...
1.e: 10, 20, 30, 40... they all end in 0.

1.q: Numbers in the 5 times table end in...
A rectangle garden is 6 m long and 4 m wide. How far is it all the way round?
1.e: Perimeter = 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 m.

1.q: A square fence has sides of 5 m. How long is the whole fence?
1.e: 4 sides x 5 m = 20 m.

1.q: Which angle is a right angle (a square corner)?
1.e: A right angle is a quarter turn, like the corner of a book or a door frame.

1.q: How many right angles are in a full turn?
1.e: A full turn is 4 quarter turns.

1.q: You face north and turn a quarter turn clockwise. Which way do you face?
1.e: Clockwise from north: east, south, west.

1.q: A bag of cement weighs 25 kg. How much do 2 bags weigh?
A bridge limit is 40 tonnes. A truck weighs 25 tonnes and carries 20 tonnes. Is it safe?
o: No - 45 tonnes is over the limit
1.e: Total weight counts: 25 + 20 = 45 tonnes, which is more than 40.

1.q: Which coins make exactly Rs 35?
You buy a Rs 45 book with a Rs 50 note. What is your change?
Which number is halfway between 20 and 30?
A train leaves with 60 people. 25 get off and 15 get on. How many now?
A bridge has 2 towers, each with 4 cables. How many cables?
1.e: 2 x 4 = 8 cables.

1.q: A clock shows 3:00. What time will it be in 2 hours?
1.e: 3 + 2 = 5 o'clock.

1.q: Which is heaviest?
1.e: 2 kg = 2000 g, the most of these.

1.q: Which is longest?
1.e: 1 m = 100 cm, longer than 99 cm.

1.q: A jug holds 2 litres. How many jugs fill a 10-litre bucket?
Which fraction is bigger?
1.e: Sharing a cake between fewer people gives bigger pieces: 1/2 is the biggest.

1.q: How many quarters make a whole?
1.e: 4 quarters = 1 whole.

1.q: A 12 m beam is cut in half. How long is each piece?
A 16 m beam is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each?
1.e: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 m. (In MODIS BridgeWorks Level 1, beams can be up to 8 m!)

1.q: Which number sentence is true?
A shape has 5 sides. What is it called?
1.e: Penta means five. A hexagon has 6, an octagon 8.

1.q: A shape has 6 sides, like a honeycomb cell. What is it?
1.e: Bees use hexagons because they fit together with no gaps and use little wax.

1.q: How many triangles are in a truss made of 5 triangles in a row, plus 1 more on top?
1.e: 5 + 1 = 6 triangles.

1.q: A worker earns Rs 10 an hour and works 8 hours. How much does he earn?
Which is the best estimate of a door's height?
1.e: A door is about 2 metres tall - taller than most people.

1.q: You have 3 shirts and 2 shorts. How many different outfits (1 shirt + 1 shorts)?
1.e: Each of 3 shirts goes with 2 shorts: 3 x 2 = 6 outfits.

1.q: What is a habitat?
o: The natural home of a plant or animal
1.e: A habitat gives a living thing food, water and shelter - like a pond for a frog.

1.q: Which habitat is very dry with little rain?
1.e: Deserts get very little rain. Cacti and camels are well suited to them.

1.q: Why does a cactus have thick stems?
1.e: Thick fleshy stems hold water for the long dry months.

1.q: Why does a cactus have spines instead of big leaves?
o: To lose less water and keep animals away
1.e: Spines lose much less water than wide leaves and protect the plant from thirsty animals.

1.q: What is a food chain?
o: A chain made of food for decoration
Who eats whom, starting from plants
1.e: Example: grass -> grasshopper -> frog -> snake. Energy passes along the chain.

1.q: Food chains almost always start with...
1.e: Plants make their own food from sunlight, so they are the producers at the start of a chain.

1.q: In grass -> rabbit -> fox, what does the rabbit eat?
1.e: The arrow means 'is eaten by': grass is eaten by the rabbit, the rabbit by the fox.

1.q: An animal that hunts other animals is called a...
1.e: Predators hunt; prey are hunted. An owl is a predator; a mouse is its prey.

1.q: Which is the life cycle of a butterfly?
1.e: This big change in shape is called metamorphosis.

1.q: Which is the life cycle of a frog?
1.e: Frog spawn hatches into tadpoles, which grow legs and become frogs.

1.q: What does a seed need to germinate (start growing)?
1.e: Most seeds wake up with water, warmth and air. Light becomes important once leaves grow.

1.q: How do some seeds travel far from the parent plant?
o: Wind, water or animals carry them
1.e: Dandelion seeds fly on the wind, coconuts float, and burrs stick to animal fur.

1.q: Why do plants need to spread their seeds far away?
o: So the new plants have space, light and water
1.e: If all seeds fell under the parent, they would compete for light and water.

1.q: What is the stem of a plant for?
o: Holding the plant up and carrying water
1.e: The stem is like a pillar with pipes inside, carrying water up from the roots.

1.q: Celery left in coloured water turns that colour at the top. What does it show?
1.e: The coloured water climbs through tiny tubes in the stem to the leaves.

1.q: How many bones does an adult human have?
1.e: Babies have about 300 bones; many join together as we grow, leaving 206.

1.q: Which is the longest bone in your body?
1.e: The femur runs from hip to knee. Its hollow tube shape makes it strong but light.

1.q: What protects your heart and lungs?
1.e: The ribs form a strong, springy cage around your chest.

1.q: Muscles work by...
o: Pulling on bones (they can only pull)
1.e: Muscles shorten to pull. To bend and straighten an arm you need two muscles working in pairs - like cables.

1.q: Where do your lungs get oxygen from?
1.e: Breathing in fills your lungs with air; oxygen passes into your blood.

1.q: What carries oxygen around your body?
1.e: Your heart pumps blood through tubes called blood vessels to every part of you.

1.q: Which food group helps you grow and repair your body?
1.e: Proteins are the building blocks your body uses for muscles and repairs.

1.q: Which food gives you quick energy?
1.e: Carbohydrates are your body's main fuel.

1.q: Why do we need fruit and vegetables?
o: Vitamins and minerals keep us healthy
1.e: Vitamins and minerals help eyes, skin, bones and fighting germs.

1.q: Milk and cheese help build strong...
1.e: They contain calcium, which bones and teeth are made of.

1.q: Why can too many sweets be bad for you?
o: Sugar can cause tooth decay and too much weight
1.e: A little is fine; lots of sugar harms teeth and health.

1.q: What are germs?
o: Tiny living things that can make us ill
1.e: Germs like bacteria and viruses are too small to see. Washing hands stops them spreading.

1.q: What does exercise do for your heart?
1.e: The heart is a muscle; exercise trains it to pump more blood with each beat.

1.q: Which animal group has feathers?
1.e: Only birds have feathers. They keep birds warm and help them fly.

1.q: Which animal group has hair or fur and feeds its babies milk?
1.e: Dogs, cows, whales and humans are all mammals.

1.q: A whale lives in the sea. Is it a fish?
o: No - it is a mammal that breathes air
1.e: Whales breathe air through a blowhole and feed their babies milk.

1.q: Which animal group lives in water and land and has moist skin?
1.e: Amphibians like frogs and newts start life in water and can later live on land.

1.q: Which has a backbone?
1.e: Animals with backbones are vertebrates. Worms, jellyfish and snails have none.

1.q: How do earthworms help the soil?
o: They mix it and let air and water in
1.e: Worm tunnels let air and water reach roots, and their waste feeds the soil.

1.q: What do bees do for flowers?
o: Carry pollen so seeds can form
1.e: Pollination by bees lets plants make fruit and seeds. Many foods depend on bees!

1.q: Why do some birds fly to warmer places in winter?
1.e: This long journey is called migration.

1.q: What is camouflage?
o: Colours or patterns that help an animal hide
1.e: A tiger's stripes blend into tall grass; a stick insect looks like a twig.

1.q: Why does a polar bear have white fur?
o: To blend in with the snow
1.e: White fur hides the bear on snow and ice so it can sneak up on seals.

1.q: Which plant part do we eat when we eat potatoes?
1.e: Potatoes are tubers - underground stems that store food for the plant.

1.q: Which plant part do we eat when we eat spinach?
1.e: Spinach and lettuce are leafy vegetables.

1.q: What do green leaves need to make food for the plant?
1.e: This process is called photosynthesis. It also gives out oxygen.

1.q: A plant kept in a dark cupboard for a week turns...
1.e: Without light the plant cannot make food or its green colour.

1.q: How do fish move through water?
o: By swishing their tails and fins
1.e: A fish's body is streamlined, and its tail pushes water back to move forward.

1.q: Why are fish shaped like a long smooth torpedo?
1.e: A streamlined shape reduces drag. Engineers shape bridge decks and trains the same way.

1.q: What does a spider use to make its web?
1.e: Spider silk is amazingly strong and stretchy for its weight.

1.q: How is a spider's web like a suspension bridge?
o: Strong threads hold weight by pulling (tension)
1.e: Both use thin strands working in tension to carry loads across a gap.

1.q: Which sense organ is the biggest?
1.e: Your skin covers your whole body and feels touch, heat, cold and pain.

1.q: Why do we have two eyes, not one?
1.e: Two eyes see slightly different views, and the brain combines them to judge depth.

1.q: Which part of your body controls everything you do?
1.e: Your brain sends messages along nerves to every part of your body.

1.q: Where does food go after you swallow it?
1.e: Food travels down a tube to the stomach, where it is broken down.

1.q: Why should we chew food well?
o: To break it into small pieces for digestion
1.e: Chewing starts digestion and makes food easier to swallow and break down.

1.q: What do baby teeth do around age 6?
o: Fall out and adult teeth grow
1.e: Milk teeth make way for bigger, permanent teeth.

1.q: Which animal is an insect?
1.e: Insects have 6 legs and 3 body parts. Spiders have 8 legs.

1.q: How do ants carry loads much heavier than themselves?
o: They are very strong for their tiny size
1.e: Small animals are strong for their size; some ants carry 10 to 50 times their own weight!

1.q: How do ants build bridges across gaps?
1.e: Army ants grip each other to form living bridges for their colony - teamwork engineering!

1.q: What do tadpoles breathe with at first?
1.e: Young tadpoles have gills like fish. Later, as frogs, they breathe with lungs and skin.

1.q: Why do trees in a forest grow tall?
o: To touch the clouds for fun
To reach the sunlight above other plants
1.e: In a crowded forest, plants compete for light, so many grow tall.

1.q: Why do tall trees have wide roots and thick trunks at the bottom?
o: To stay standing in strong winds
1.e: Like a tower, a tree needs a strong wide base so the wind cannot tip it over.

1.q: What do we call animals that are active at night?
1.e: Owls, bats and foxes are nocturnal - they sleep in the day.

1.q: What happens to your body when you are scared?
o: Your heart beats faster to get ready to run
1.e: Fear prepares your body for action - the heart pumps faster to feed your muscles.

1.q: Which helps keep your body temperature down when you are hot?
1.e: Sweat evaporates from your skin and takes heat away with it.

1.q: What is the normal human body temperature?
1.e: A healthy body stays near 37 °C. A higher temperature is a fever.

1.q: Why do we have eyebrows?
o: To stop sweat and rain running into our eyes
1.e: Eyebrows guide sweat and water to the sides, away from your eyes.

1.q: Which helps you balance?
1.e: Tiny fluid-filled tubes in your inner ear sense movement and tilt.

1.q: Which is a renewable natural material from plants?
1.e: Bamboo regrows quickly and is strong - it is even used for scaffolding and bridges.

1.q: What do mushrooms belong to?
o: Plants that make food from light
1.e: Fungi get food from rotting material; they cannot make food from sunlight.

1.q: What do decomposers like fungi and worms do?
o: Break down dead things into soil
1.e: Decomposers recycle dead leaves and animals back into nutrients for new plants.

1.q: Why do wooden bridges need protection from some fungi and insects?
o: They can rot or eat the wood and weaken it
1.e: Rot fungi and termites can weaken timber, so it is treated and kept dry.

1.q: Which animal eats wood and can damage wooden buildings?
1.e: Termites chew through wood. Builders treat timber to keep them out.

1.q: What do roots do besides holding the plant?
1.e: Roots soak up water and minerals from the soil and send them up the stem.

1.q: Why do riverbanks with plant roots wash away less in floods?
1.e: A mat of roots binds soil like steel bars in concrete - engineers plant banks near bridges for this reason.

1.q: Which animal sheds its skin as it grows?
1.e: Snakes grow a new skin underneath and wriggle out of the old one.

1.q: Why do people wash cuts and cover them with a plaster?
