5.e: One male gamete fuses with the egg; the other fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the food-storing endosperm.

5.q: Which is a barrier method of contraception that also protects against sexually transmitted infections?
5.e: Pills, IUDs and sterilisation prevent pregnancy but not infections such as HIV.

5.q: Which cells does HIV mainly attack?
5.e: Loss of helper T cells cripples both antibody and cell-mediated immunity, leading to AIDS.

5.q: Vaccination gives protection mainly by producing…
5.e: This is active immunity; injecting ready-made antibodies (as for snakebite) is passive immunity.

5.q: Which antibody crosses the placenta to protect the foetus?
5.e: IgA protects the newborn through colostrum; IgE is involved in allergies.

5.q: Malaria is caused by…
o: The protozoan Plasmodium, spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes
A virus spread by Aedes mosquitoes
5.e: Plasmodium multiplies in the liver and red blood cells; the rupture of red cells causes the cycles of fever.

5.q: Cancer cells differ from normal cells because they…
o: Lose contact inhibition and divide without control
5.e: Mutations in oncogenes and tumour-suppressor genes remove the normal brakes on division.

5.q: Restriction enzymes such as EcoRI are used in genetic engineering to…
o: Cut DNA at specific recognition sequences
5.e: Many leave 'sticky ends' that pair with any DNA cut by the same enzyme; DNA ligase then seals the joint.

5.q: Why is Taq polymerase used in PCR?
o: It works only at room temperature
It survives the high temperatures used to separate DNA strands
5.e: It comes from Thermus aquaticus, a bacterium of hot springs, and is not destroyed at about 94°C.

5.q: Bt cotton resists bollworms because it carries a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis that makes…
o: A Cry protein toxic to insect larvae
5.e: The protoxin becomes active only in the alkaline gut of certain insects, so it is harmless to humans.

5.q: Human insulin is now produced mainly by…
o: Recombinant DNA technology in bacteria or yeast
Extracting it from pig pancreas only
5.e: Eli Lilly made the A and B chains in E. coli in 1983 and joined them by disulphide bonds.

5.q: DNA fingerprinting is based on differences between people in…
5.e: These short repeated sequences vary in length from person to person, giving a unique band pattern.

5.q: In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the anode because…
o: They are attracted by the gel
5.e: The phosphate backbone carries negative charge; smaller fragments move faster through the gel.

5.q: Which gas is the main component of biogas?
5.e: Methanogenic archaea in cattle dung digest organic matter without oxygen, giving 50-70% methane.

5.q: Penicillin was discovered from…
5.e: Fleming noticed in 1928 that the mould killed Staphylococcus colonies; Florey and Chain made it a medicine.

5.q: Ecological succession that starts on bare rock with no soil is called…
5.e: Lichens are the pioneers; secondary succession starts where soil remains, such as on abandoned farmland.

5.q: Which ecological pyramid can never be inverted?
o: All of them can be inverted
5.e: Energy is lost at every transfer; a single tree with many insects inverts the number pyramid, and oceans invert biomass.

5.q: Which region of India is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots?
5.e: India shares four hotspots: the Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, the Himalaya, Indo-Burma and Sundaland.

5.q: Excess nitrates and phosphates from farms entering a lake cause…
o: Eutrophication and algal blooms that use up oxygen
5.e: Dead algae decompose, raising the BOD; fish can die from lack of oxygen.

5.q: Which kind of interaction benefits one species and leaves the other unaffected?
5.e: An orchid growing on a mango branch gets light and support; the tree is neither helped nor harmed.

5.q: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that…
o: Two species competing for exactly the same resources cannot coexist indefinitely
All species can share any niche
5.e: One species eventually wins unless they divide the resource (resource partitioning).

5.q: A population growing with limited resources follows which curve?
o: Logistic, S-shaped, levelling off at the carrying capacity K
5.e: dN/dt = rN(K - N)/K: growth slows as N approaches K.

5.q: Which enzyme in saliva begins the digestion of starch?
5.e: It breaks starch into maltose at a near-neutral pH; stomach acid stops it.

5.q: Bile from the liver helps digestion by…
5.e: Bile salts increase the surface area for pancreatic lipase; bile contains no digestive enzymes.

5.q: Which vitamin deficiency causes night blindness?
5.e: Vitamin A forms retinal, part of the rod pigment rhodopsin needed for dim-light vision.

5.q: An enzyme's activity drops when a molecule resembling its substrate occupies the active site. This is…
5.e: Adding more substrate can overcome it; malonate inhibiting succinate dehydrogenase is the classic case.

5.q: At which stage of mitosis do chromosomes line up at the cell's equator?
5.e: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores; chromosomes are easiest to count at this stage.

5.q: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes happens during…
o: Pachytene of prophase I of meiosis
5.e: Paired homologues exchange segments at chiasmata, creating new allele combinations.

5.q: Which organelle is called the 'suicide bag' of the cell?
5.e: It holds hydrolytic enzymes that can digest worn-out parts - or the whole cell if it bursts.

5.q: Which organelles contain their own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes, supporting the endosymbiotic theory?
5.e: They resemble bacteria and divide by fission, suggesting they were once free-living prokaryotes.

5.q: The fluid mosaic model describes the cell membrane as…
o: A phospholipid bilayer with proteins that can move within it
5.e: Singer and Nicolson (1972): proteins float like icebergs in a sea of lipid.

5.q: Glucose enters many cells down its concentration gradient through carrier proteins without using ATP. This is…
5.e: Carriers speed up diffusion; active transport, such as the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, moves substances against the gradient using ATP.

5.q: Which class of animals has a four-chambered heart and is warm-blooded but lays eggs?
5.e: Birds and mammals are endothermic with fully separated circulations; crocodiles also have four chambers but are cold-blooded.

5.q: Which kingdom in Whittaker's five-kingdom system contains unicellular eukaryotes such as Amoeba and Euglena?
5.e: Monera holds the prokaryotes (bacteria); Fungi, Plantae and Animalia are multicellular eukaryotes.

5.q: Which statement about viruses is correct?
o: They can reproduce only inside living host cells
They have both DNA and RNA always
5.e: Outside a cell a virus is an inert particle; antibiotics target bacterial structures that viruses lack.

5.q: In-vitro fertilisation (IVF) means…
o: Fertilisation outside the body, followed by embryo transfer
5.e: The embryo is placed in the uterus (or the zygote in the fallopian tube, ZIFT) to develop normally.

5.q: Which hormone from the pancreas raises blood glucose between meals?
5.e: Glucagon from α cells makes the liver break down glycogen; insulin from β cells lowers blood glucose.

5.q: Which gland is called the 'master gland' because it controls several other endocrine glands?
5.e: Its own secretion is in turn controlled by releasing hormones from the hypothalamus.

5.q: Iodine deficiency in the diet commonly causes…
5.e: Without iodine the thyroid cannot make thyroxine; TSH keeps stimulating it and it swells. Iodised salt prevents it.

5.q: What is the main role of the ozone layer in the stratosphere?
o: It traps heat to warm the Earth
5.e: Thinning ozone raises the risk of skin cancer and cataracts; the Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs.

5.q: Which group of organisms fixes atmospheric nitrogen in rice paddies?
5.e: They are used as biofertilisers; Anabaena also lives inside the water fern Azolla.

5.q: Which blood cells are the first to arrive at a site of infection and engulf bacteria?
5.e: Neutrophils are the most common white cells; pus is largely dead neutrophils and bacteria.

5.q: A person of blood group O is called a 'universal donor' because their red cells…
o: Carry neither A nor B antigens
Carry both A and B antigens
5.e: Recipients' anti-A and anti-B antibodies have nothing to attack; AB people are universal recipients.

5.q: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when…
o: An Rh-negative mother carries a second Rh-positive baby
5.e: Antibodies made after the first birth cross the placenta and destroy the baby's red cells; anti-D injections prevent it.

5.q: Which part of the brain coordinates balance and fine movements?
5.e: The medulla controls breathing and heartbeat; the hypothalamus controls temperature, hunger and thirst.

5.q: In the eye, which cells are responsible for colour vision?
5.e: Three kinds of cones respond to red, green and blue light; rods work in dim light and see only shades of grey.

5.q: Which part of a flower develops into the fruit after fertilisation?
5.e: The ovules become seeds; fruits that develop without fertilisation (parthenocarpy) are seedless, like bananas.

5.q: Which part of a neuron receives signals from other neurons?
5.e: Signals travel dendrites → cell body → axon → axon terminals, where neurotransmitters cross the synapse.

5.q: A reflex action such as pulling a hand away from a flame is coordinated by…
5.e: The reflex arc (receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → muscle) skips the brain for speed.

5.q: Which hormone from the adrenal medulla prepares the body for 'fight or flight'?
5.e: It raises heart rate, blood glucose and blood flow to muscles within seconds.

5.q: Which hormone keeps the uterine lining ready for pregnancy after ovulation?
5.e: It is made by the corpus luteum; when it falls, the lining breaks down and menstruation begins.

5.q: Which structure in the testes secretes testosterone?
5.e: Sertoli cells nourish developing sperm; the epididymis stores and matures them.

5.q: Which type of RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome?
5.e: Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with a codon on the mRNA.

5.q: Reverse transcriptase, found in retroviruses such as HIV, makes…
5.e: It reverses the usual flow of the central dogma; scientists use it to make cDNA from mRNA.

5.q: Plasmids are useful vectors in genetic engineering because they…
o: Replicate independently inside bacteria and can carry foreign genes
Are found only in the nucleus of plants
5.e: Good vectors also have an origin of replication, selectable markers such as antibiotic-resistance genes, and cloning sites.

5.q: Golden rice was engineered to fight…
5.e: It makes β-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, in its grain.

5.q: ELISA tests detect infections by using…
o: Antigen-antibody reactions linked to an enzyme colour change
5.e: It can detect HIV antibodies or viral antigens even before symptoms appear.

5.q: Which of these is an example of ex-situ conservation?
o: A seed bank or botanical garden
5.e: Ex-situ means outside the natural habitat; national parks and sanctuaries protect species in place (in-situ).

5.q: The 'evil quartet' of causes of biodiversity loss includes habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species invasion and…
5.e: When a host goes extinct, its specialised parasites and partners vanish with it.

5.q: Which greenhouse gas is released in large amounts by rice paddies and cattle?
5.e: Methane traps much more heat per molecule than CO₂, though it stays in the air for less time.

5.q: Biomagnification means that a persistent pollutant such as DDT…
o: Becomes more concentrated at each higher trophic level
5.e: Fish-eating birds had DDT levels millions of times higher than the water, making their eggshells thin.

5.q: Which tissue is responsible for increasing the girth (secondary growth) of a dicot stem?
5.e: Cambium adds xylem inside and phloem outside; the yearly layers of xylem form annual rings.

5.q: Stomata open when guard cells…
o: Take in water and become turgid
5.e: K⁺ ions flow in, water follows by osmosis, and the thick inner walls make the cells curve apart.

5.q: Which pigment is the main photosynthetic pigment in green plants?
5.e: Chlorophyll a forms the reaction centres of both photosystems; the others are accessory pigments.

5.q: Which statement about anaerobic respiration in human muscles is correct?
o: It gives more ATP than aerobic respiration
Pyruvate is turned into lactic acid when oxygen runs short
5.e: It gives only 2 ATP per glucose; yeast instead makes ethanol and CO₂.

5.q: Which component of blood is mainly responsible for clotting?
5.e: Platelets release factors that turn prothrombin into thrombin, which turns fibrinogen into a fibrin mesh.

5.q: Which organ produces bile?
5.e: The gall bladder only stores and concentrates bile made by the liver.

5.q: Which vitamin is made by the skin in sunlight and helps absorb calcium?
5.e: Its lack causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.

5.q: Which statement describes a test cross?
o: Crossing an individual of dominant phenotype with a homozygous recessive
5.e: If any offspring show the recessive trait, the tested parent must be heterozygous.

5.q: Which statement about Mendel's law of independent assortment is correct?
o: It applies to genes close together on the same chromosome
Alleles of different genes separate independently during gamete formation
All genes are always inherited together
Dominant alleles always pair with dominant alleles
5.e: It holds for genes on different chromosomes (or far apart on one), giving the 9:3:3:1 ratio.

5.q: Which statement about the human genome project's findings is correct?
o: Less than 2% of the genome codes for proteins
All human DNA codes for proteins
5.e: There are about 20,000-25,000 genes; much of the rest is regulatory or repetitive DNA.

5.q: A deposit pays 12% a year compounded monthly. What is the effective annual rate?
5.e: EAR = (1 + 12%/12)^12 - 1 = 12.68%. More frequent compounding raises the true yield.

5.q: A deposit pays 10% a year compounded quarterly. What is the effective annual rate?
5.e: EAR = (1 + 10%/4)^4 - 1 = 10.38%. More frequent compounding raises the true yield.

5.q: A deposit pays 8% a year compounded half-yearly. What is the effective annual rate?
5.e: EAR = (1 + 8%/2)^2 - 1 = 8.16%. More frequent compounding raises the true yield.

5.q: What is the effective annual rate of 10% a year compounded continuously?
5.e: EAR = e^0.1 - 1 = 10.52% - the upper limit of compounding more and more often.

5.q: What is the effective annual rate of 6% a year compounded continuously?
5.e: EAR = e^0.06 - 1 = 6.18% - the upper limit of compounding more and more often.

5.q: Rs 10,000 is invested at 10% a year compound interest. What is it worth after 3 years?
Rs 50,000 is invested at 8% a year compound interest. What is it worth after 5 years?
How much must be invested today at 10% compound interest to have Rs 12,100 in 2 years?
How much must be invested today at 8% compound interest to have Rs 100,000 in 5 years?
Using the rule of 72, roughly how many years does money take to double at 8% a year?
5.e: 72 ÷ 8 = 9 years; the exact answer is ln 2 ÷ ln(1 + r).

5.q: Using the rule of 72, roughly how many years does money take to double at 6% a year?
5.e: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years; the exact answer is ln 2 ÷ ln(1 + r).

5.q: Rs 1,000 is deposited at the end of every year for 3 years at 10% interest. What is the total at the end?
5.e: FV of an ordinary annuity = A[(1 + r)ⁿ - 1] ÷ r = Rs 3,310.

5.q: Rs 5,000 is deposited at the end of every year for 10 years at 8% interest. What is the total at the end?
5.e: FV of an ordinary annuity = A[(1 + r)ⁿ - 1] ÷ r = Rs 72,432.81.

5.q: What is the present value of Rs 10,000 received at the end of each year for 2 years, at 10%?
What is the present value of Rs 20,000 received at the end of each year for 5 years, at 8%?
A lease needs Rs 10,000 at the START of each year for 3 years. At 10%, what is its present value?
5.e: An annuity due is an ordinary annuity x (1 + r): Rs 27,355.37.

5.q: A lease needs Rs 25,000 at the START of each year for 5 years. At 8%, what is its present value?
5.e: An annuity due is an ordinary annuity x (1 + r): Rs 107,803.17.

5.q: An endowment pays Rs 5,000 a year forever. At a discount rate of 8%, what is it worth today?
5.e: Perpetuity value = C ÷ r = 5,000 ÷ 0.08 = Rs 62,500.

5.q: An endowment pays Rs 12,000 a year forever. At a discount rate of 6%, what is it worth today?
5.e: Perpetuity value = C ÷ r = 12,000 ÷ 0.06 = Rs 200,000.

5.q: A payment of Rs 2,000 next year will grow at 4% a year forever. At 10%, what is it worth today?
5.e: Growing perpetuity = C ÷ (r - g) = 2,000 ÷ 0.06 = Rs 33,333.33.

5.q: A payment of Rs 5,000 next year will grow at 7% a year forever. At 12%, what is it worth today?
5.e: Growing perpetuity = C ÷ (r - g) = 5,000 ÷ 0.05 = Rs 100,000.

5.q: A loan of Rs 100,000 at 12% a year is repaid in 12 equal monthly instalments. What is the EMI?
A loan of Rs 500,000 at 9% a year is repaid in 60 equal monthly instalments. What is the EMI?
In the first month of a Rs 3,000,000 home loan at 9% a year, how much of the EMI is interest?
5.e: Interest = outstanding balance x monthly rate = 3,000,000 x 9%/12 = Rs 22,500; the rest of the EMI repays principal.

5.q: In the first month of a Rs 1,200,000 home loan at 8% a year, how much of the EMI is interest?
5.e: Interest = outstanding balance x monthly rate = 1,200,000 x 8%/12 = Rs 8,000; the rest of the EMI repays principal.

5.q: A company must have Rs 500,000 in 5 years to replace a machine. With 10% interest, how much should it set aside each year?
5.e: Sinking fund A = F r ÷ [(1 + r)ⁿ - 1] = Rs 81,898.74.

5.q: A company must have Rs 2,000,000 in 10 years to replace a machine. With 8% interest, how much should it set aside each year?
5.e: Sinking fund A = F r ÷ [(1 + r)ⁿ - 1] = Rs 138,058.98.

5.q: A machine costs Rs 110,000, has a salvage value of Rs 10,000 and a life of 4 years. What is the first year's depreciation by the sum-of-years'-digits method?
5.e: Digits sum to 10; year 1 takes 4/10 of 100,000 = Rs 40,000.

5.q: A machine costs Rs 500,000, has a salvage value of Rs 50,000 and a life of 5 years. What is the first year's depreciation by the sum-of-years'-digits method?
5.e: Digits sum to 15; year 1 takes 5/15 of 450,000 = Rs 150,000.

5.q: An asset costing Rs 200,000 with a 5-year life is depreciated by the double-declining-balance method. What is the first year's charge?
An asset costing Rs 90,000 with a 4-year life is depreciated by the double-declining-balance method. What is the first year's charge?
A footbridge costs Rs 2,000,000 to build and Rs 50,000 a year to maintain forever. At 8%, what is its capitalised cost?
A footbridge costs Rs 5,000,000 to build and Rs 100,000 a year to maintain forever. At 10%, what is its capitalised cost?
A machine costs Rs 100 now and brings Rs 60 after one year and Rs 60 after two. At 10%, what is the NPV?
A machine costs Rs 1,000 now and brings Rs 600 after one year and Rs 700 after two. At 12%, what is the NPV?
A share will pay a dividend of Rs 5 next year, growing at 7% a year. Investors want 12%. What is the share worth?
5.e: Gordon growth model: P = D₁ ÷ (k - g) = 5 ÷ 0.05 = Rs 100.

5.q: A share will pay a dividend of Rs 8 next year, growing at 6% a year. Investors want 14%. What is the share worth?
5.e: Gordon growth model: P = D₁ ÷ (k - g) = 8 ÷ 0.08 = Rs 100.

5.q: The risk-free rate is 6%, the market return is 12% and a share's beta is 1.2. What return does CAPM require?
The risk-free rate is 7%, the market return is 13% and a share's beta is 0.8. What return does CAPM require?
A firm has Rs 60 crore of equity costing 15% and Rs 40 crore of debt at 10%; the tax rate is 30%. What is its WACC?
A firm has Rs 70 crore of equity costing 14% and Rs 30 crore of debt at 9%; the tax rate is 25%. What is its WACC?
A company borrows at 10% and pays tax at 30%. What is its after-tax cost of debt?
5.e: Interest is tax-deductible: 10 x (1 - 0.3) = 7%.

5.q: A company borrows at 12% and pays tax at 25%. What is its after-tax cost of debt?
5.e: Interest is tax-deductible: 12 x (1 - 0.25) = 9%.

5.q: A bond paying Rs 80 a year in coupons trades at Rs 950. What is its current yield?
5.e: Current yield = annual coupon ÷ price = 80 ÷ 950 = 8.42%.

5.q: A bond paying Rs 70 a year in coupons trades at Rs 1,050. What is its current yield?
5.e: Current yield = annual coupon ÷ price = 70 ÷ 1,050 = 6.67%.

5.q: A 2-year bond of face value Rs 1,000 pays a 8% annual coupon. If the market yield is 10%, what is its price?
5.e: Discount each coupon and the face value at 10%: Rs 965.29 - below par because the yield is above the coupon.

5.q: A 2-year bond of face value Rs 1,000 pays a 10% annual coupon. If the market yield is 8%, what is its price?
5.e: Discount each coupon and the face value at 8%: Rs 1,035.67 - above par because the yield is below the coupon.

5.q: A company's contribution is Rs 500 lakh and its operating profit (EBIT) is Rs 200 lakh. What is its degree of operating leverage?
5.e: DOL = contribution ÷ EBIT = 500 ÷ 200 = 2.5: a 1% rise in sales lifts EBIT by 2.5%.

5.q: A company's contribution is Rs 900 lakh and its operating profit (EBIT) is Rs 300 lakh. What is its degree of operating leverage?
5.e: DOL = contribution ÷ EBIT = 900 ÷ 300 = 3: a 1% rise in sales lifts EBIT by 3%.

5.q: A firm has EBIT of Rs 200 lakh and interest of Rs 50 lakh. What is its degree of financial leverage?
5.e: DFL = EBIT ÷ (EBIT - interest) = 200 ÷ 150 = 1.33.

5.q: A firm has EBIT of Rs 400 lakh and interest of Rs 160 lakh. What is its degree of financial leverage?
5.e: DFL = EBIT ÷ (EBIT - interest) = 400 ÷ 240 = 1.67.

5.q: A company has a net profit margin of 5%, asset turnover of 2 and an equity multiplier of 1.5. What is its return on equity?
5.e: DuPont: ROE = margin x turnover x multiplier = 5 x 2 x 1.5 = 15%.

5.q: A company has a net profit margin of 8%, asset turnover of 1.2 and an equity multiplier of 2. What is its return on equity?
5.e: DuPont: ROE = margin x turnover x multiplier = 8 x 1.2 x 2 = 19.2%.

5.q: A firm has current assets of Rs 500 lakh (including inventory of Rs 200 lakh) and current liabilities of Rs 250 lakh. What is its quick ratio?
5.e: Quick ratio = (current assets - inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 300 ÷ 250 = 1.2.

5.q: A firm has current assets of Rs 800 lakh (including inventory of Rs 300 lakh) and current liabilities of Rs 400 lakh. What is its quick ratio?
5.e: Quick ratio = (current assets - inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 500 ÷ 400 = 1.25.

5.q: A cement dealer's inventory turns over 8 times a year. On average, how many days does stock stay in the warehouse?
5.e: Days in inventory = 365 ÷ turnover = 365 ÷ 8 = 45.62 days.

5.q: A cement dealer's inventory turns over 12 times a year. On average, how many days does stock stay in the warehouse?
5.e: Days in inventory = 365 ÷ turnover = 365 ÷ 12 = 30.42 days.

5.q: A company earns Rs 25 per share and similar firms trade at a P/E ratio of 18. What price does that suggest?
5.e: Price = EPS x P/E = 25 x 18 = Rs 450.

5.q: A company earns Rs 42.5 per share and similar firms trade at a P/E ratio of 22. What price does that suggest?
5.e: Price = EPS x P/E = 42.5 x 22 = Rs 935.

5.q: A precast-block plant has fixed costs of Rs 300,000 a month, sells blocks at Rs 50 and spends Rs 30 on each. How many blocks a month must it sell to break even?
5.e: Break-even = fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit = 300,000 ÷ (50 - 30) = 15,000 blocks.

5.q: A precast-block plant has fixed costs of Rs 450,000 a month, sells blocks at Rs 120 and spends Rs 75 on each. How many blocks a month must it sell to break even?
5.e: Break-even = fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit = 450,000 ÷ (120 - 75) = 10,000 blocks.

5.q: A firm sells 10,000 units a month and breaks even at 8,000 units. What is its margin of safety?
5.e: (actual - break-even) ÷ actual = 2,000 ÷ 10,000 = 20%: sales can fall this much before losses start.

5.q: A firm sells 25,000 units a month and breaks even at 15,000 units. What is its margin of safety?
5.e: (actual - break-even) ÷ actual = 10,000 ÷ 25,000 = 40%: sales can fall this much before losses start.

5.q: A portfolio holds 60% in a fund expected to earn 12% and the rest in one expected to earn 7%. What is its expected return?
5.e: Weighted average: 0.6 x 12 + 0.4 x 7 = 10%.

5.q: A portfolio holds 30% in a fund expected to earn 15% and the rest in one expected to earn 8%. What is its expected return?
5.e: Weighted average: 0.3 x 15 + 0.7 x 8 = 10.1%.

5.q: Two uncorrelated assets have standard deviations of 20% and 20%. What is the standard deviation of a portfolio with 50% in the first?
5.e: With zero correlation σp = √(w₁²σ₁² + w₂²σ₂²) = 14.14% - lower than either asset alone: diversification.

5.q: Two uncorrelated assets have standard deviations of 15% and 25%. What is the standard deviation of a portfolio with 60% in the first?
5.e: With zero correlation σp = √(w₁²σ₁² + w₂²σ₂²) = 13.45% - lower than either asset alone: diversification.

5.q: A fund returned 14% with a standard deviation of 16% while the risk-free rate was 6%. What is its Sharpe ratio?
5.e: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) ÷ σ = (14 - 6) ÷ 16 = 0.5: excess return per unit of risk.

5.q: A fund returned 11% with a standard deviation of 10% while the risk-free rate was 5%. What is its Sharpe ratio?
5.e: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) ÷ σ = (11 - 5) ÷ 10 = 0.6: excess return per unit of risk.

5.q: A share trades at Rs 100; a one-year call with strike Rs 100 costs Rs 12 and the interest rate is 10%. By put-call parity, what should the matching put cost?
A share trades at Rs 250; a one-year call with strike Rs 240 costs Rs 30 and the interest rate is 8%. By put-call parity, what should the matching put cost?
An investor buys a call option with strike Rs 100 for a premium of Rs 12. At expiry the share is at Rs 130. What is the profit per share?
5.e: Payoff = max(S - K, 0) = 30; profit = payoff - premium = Rs 18.

5.q: An investor buys a call option with strike Rs 100 for a premium of Rs 8. At expiry the share is at Rs 120. What is the profit per share?
5.e: Payoff = max(S - K, 0) = 20; profit = payoff - premium = Rs 12.

5.q: A fixed deposit pays 10% while inflation is 4%. What is the exact real rate of return?
5.e: (1 + 0.1) ÷ (1 + 0.04) - 1 = 5.77% - a little below the simple difference 6%.

5.q: A fixed deposit pays 7% while inflation is 5%. What is the exact real rate of return?
5.e: (1 + 0.07) ÷ (1 + 0.05) - 1 = 1.9% - a little below the simple difference 2%.

5.q: The rupee-dollar spot rate is Rs 83 per $. Rupee interest is 7% and dollar interest is 4%. What should the one-year forward rate be (Rs per $)?
5.e: Interest rate parity: F = S x (1 + i_INR) ÷ (1 + i_USD) = 83 x 1.07 ÷ 1.04 = Rs 85.39.

5.q: The rupee-dollar spot rate is Rs 80 per $. Rupee interest is 6.5% and dollar interest is 5%. What should the one-year forward rate be (Rs per $)?
5.e: Interest rate parity: F = S x (1 + i_INR) ÷ (1 + i_USD) = 80 x 1.065 ÷ 1.05 = Rs 81.14.

5.q: If banks must keep 4% of deposits as reserves and lend all the rest, what is the maximum money multiplier?
5.e: Money multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio = 1 ÷ 0.04 = 25.

5.q: If banks must keep 5% of deposits as reserves and lend all the rest, what is the maximum money multiplier?
5.e: Money multiplier = 1 ÷ reserve ratio = 1 ÷ 0.05 = 20.

5.q: For the same nominal rate, which compounding gives the largest amount after one year?
5.e: The more often interest is added, the more interest earns interest; continuous compounding is the limit.

5.q: How does an annuity due differ from an ordinary annuity?
o: Payments come at the start of each period, so it is worth (1 + r) times more
Payments come at the end of each period
5.e: Rent paid in advance is an annuity due; loan EMIs paid in arrears form an ordinary annuity.

5.q: Over the life of an equal-instalment loan, the interest portion of each EMI…
o: Falls, while the principal portion rises
Is zero in the first year
5.e: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance, which shrinks with every payment.

5.q: Why do companies like accelerated depreciation methods for tax purposes?
o: They increase total depreciation over the asset's life
They raise reported profit early on
Larger early deductions defer tax, which is worth more today
5.e: Total depreciation is the same, but tax saved sooner has a higher present value.

5.q: Depreciation itself is a non-cash expense. How does it still affect cash flow?
o: It has no effect at all
It lowers taxable profit and so lowers tax paid
It is paid to the bank each year
5.e: The depreciation tax shield = depreciation x tax rate.

5.q: When market interest rates rise, the prices of existing fixed-coupon bonds…
5.e: New bonds pay more, so old ones must get cheaper to offer the same yield.

5.q: A bond's duration measures…
o: How sensitive its price is to interest-rate changes
5.e: Longer duration means bigger price swings; zero-coupon bonds have duration equal to maturity.

5.q: What does an inverted yield curve (short-term rates above long-term rates) often signal?
5.e: Markets expect rates to fall later, as they usually do in a downturn.

5.q: A share with a beta of 1.5 is expected to…
o: Move about 1.5 times as much as the market
Move half as much as the market
5.e: Beta measures systematic risk; the market itself has a beta of 1.

5.q: Which risk can be removed by holding a well-diversified portfolio?
5.e: A strike at one firm is offset by others; risks that hit the whole market remain.

5.q: The efficient frontier shows…
o: Portfolios with the highest return for each level of risk
5.e: Rational investors pick a point on it according to how much risk they can bear.

5.q: The semi-strong form of the efficient market hypothesis says that prices reflect…
5.e: Then neither chart reading nor studying published accounts can beat the market consistently.

5.q: What is arbitrage?
o: A riskless profit from price differences for the same asset
5.e: Buying cheap in one market and selling dear in another quickly removes the gap.

5.q: The buyer of a put option has…
o: The right, but not the obligation, to sell at the strike price
The right to buy at the strike price
5.e: A put gains when the price falls - like insurance on a share you own.

5.q: What is the intrinsic value of a call option with strike Rs 100 when the share is at Rs 90?
o: Zero (it is out of the money)
5.e: Exercising would mean paying 100 for something worth 90; any premium left is pure time value.

5.q: How do futures differ from forward contracts?
o: Futures are private deals with no exchange
Futures are standardised, exchange-traded and settled daily (marked to market)
5.e: Daily settlement through a clearing house almost removes the risk that the other side defaults.

5.q: In an interest-rate swap, two parties typically exchange…
o: Currencies at a fixed rate only
5.e: A company with a floating loan can swap into fixed payments to make its costs predictable.

5.q: What is the repo rate in India?
o: The rate on government bonds only
The rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to banks
The rate banks pay on savings accounts
5.e: Raising the repo rate makes borrowing dearer across the economy and helps control inflation.

5.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requires Indian banks to…
o: Hold a share of deposits in safe liquid assets such as government securities
5.e: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the part kept as cash with the RBI itself.

5.q: An IPO is…
o: A company's first sale of shares to the public
5.e: After listing, the shares trade between investors in the secondary market.

5.q: What is the NAV of a mutual fund?
o: The market value of its assets minus liabilities, per unit
5.e: Units are bought and redeemed at the NAV, which is worked out every business day.

5.q: Why does investing a fixed sum every month (SIP) lower the average cost per unit?
o: The same rupees buy more units when prices are low
Units are sold at a discount to SIP investors
Prices never fall during an SIP
5.e: This 'rupee-cost averaging' makes the average purchase price below the average market price.

5.q: According to Modigliani and Miller (no taxes, perfect markets), a firm's value…
o: Does not depend on how it mixes debt and equity
Rises with every rupee of debt
5.e: With corporate taxes, debt adds value through the tax shield - until distress costs take over.

5.q: Free cash flow to the firm is roughly…
o: Operating cash flow minus capital spending
5.e: It is the cash available to all investors after the business keeps its assets running and growing.

5.q: EBITDA stands for earnings before…
5.e: It roughly measures cash profit from operations, before financing and accounting charges.

5.q: A company's cash conversion cycle shortens when it…
o: Collects from customers faster and pays suppliers later
5.e: Cycle = inventory days + receivable days - payable days; a shorter cycle needs less working capital.

5.q: What is factoring?
o: Selling receivables to a finance company for cash now
Splitting a share into smaller ones
5.e: A contractor waiting 90 days for a government bill can get most of the money immediately, at a discount.

5.q: A letter of credit protects an exporter because…
o: The buyer pays in advance always
A bank promises to pay once the shipping documents are presented
5.e: The seller relies on the bank's credit rather than on an unknown foreign buyer.

5.q: A credit rating of 'AAA' on a bond means…
o: It is a government tax bond
The highest safety - the lowest chance of default
5.e: Lower ratings (BB and below are 'junk') must pay higher interest to attract buyers.

5.q: What does a company's book value per share measure?
o: Shareholders' equity on the balance sheet divided by the number of shares
5.e: A price-to-book ratio above 1 means investors value the business above its accounting net worth.

5.q: A bonus issue of shares (1 free share for every 1 held)…
o: Doubles the number of shares but does not change the company's total value
Raises new cash for the company
5.e: Reserves are converted into share capital; the share price roughly halves.

5.q: A company buys back its own shares. What usually happens to earnings per share?
o: It rises, because profit is shared among fewer shares
5.e: Buybacks return cash to shareholders, like a dividend but with different tax effects.

5.q: Fiscal deficit means…
o: The RBI prints too little money
The government's total spending exceeds its total receipts excluding borrowing
5.e: It shows how much the government must borrow in the year.

5.q: If the rupee depreciates against the dollar, an Indian firm importing steel will find that…
o: Its imports cost more in rupees
Its imports cost less in rupees
5.e: Exporters gain instead, because their dollar earnings convert into more rupees.

5.q: Which is an example of a 'hedge' for an Indian company that must pay $1 million in six months?
o: Buying dollars forward today at a fixed rate
Selling all its rupees now for gold
5.e: The forward locks the cost; the company gives up any gain if the rupee strengthens.

5.q: What is the main purpose of Ind AS / IFRS accounting standards?
o: To make financial statements comparable and transparent across companies
5.e: Common rules let investors compare firms fairly, including foreign investors.

5.q: In capital budgeting, mutually exclusive projects are…
o: Alternatives where choosing one rules out the others
Projects that can all be done together
5.e: For example, a steel or a concrete design for the same bridge; pick the one with the higher NPV.

5.q: When should a project's cash flows be adjusted for inflation?
o: Always discount nominal cash flows at a nominal rate (or real at real) - never mix them
5.e: Mixing a nominal rate with real cash flows understates the project's value, and the reverse overstates it.

5.q: What does a high debt-to-equity ratio indicate?
o: The company relies heavily on borrowed money and carries more financial risk
5.e: It magnifies returns in good years and losses in bad ones.

5.q: The interest coverage ratio (EBIT ÷ interest) of 1.2 suggests…
o: The firm barely earns enough to pay its interest
5.e: Lenders usually want 2-3 or more; below 1 means operating profit does not even cover interest.

5.q: Why might a profitable company still run out of cash?
o: Its money is tied up in unpaid customer bills and stock
5.e: Fast-growing contractors often fail this way: work is billed, but cash arrives months later.

5.q: A 'stop-loss' order on a share…
o: Sells automatically if the price falls to a set level
Buys more when the price falls
Stops all trading in the share
5.e: It limits the loss on a position, though in a sudden crash it may fill below the set price.

5.q: Which is a feature of a zero-coupon bond?
o: It pays no interest but is sold at a deep discount to face value
It always trades above face value
5.e: The investor's return is the difference between the purchase price and the face value at maturity.

5.q: What is the 'time value' part of an option's premium?
o: The extra paid for the chance the option gains value before expiry
5.e: It shrinks as expiry approaches and is zero at expiry.

5.q: Which statement about simple and compound interest over several years is true?
o: Compound interest is less after many years
Compound interest is always more than simple interest at the same rate for more than one year
5.e: From the second year compound interest also earns interest on earlier interest.

5.q: Which is the best measure of a firm's ability to pay its short-term bills without selling stock?
5.e: It leaves out inventory, which may be slow to turn into cash.

5.q: A company's shares trade at a very high P/E ratio. This usually means investors…
o: Think the company will soon close
5.e: They pay many years of current earnings now, betting on growth; a high P/E can also mean the share is overpriced.

5.q: Why does a business keep a cash budget?
o: To foresee shortfalls and arrange finance before bills fall due
5.e: It lists expected cash receipts and payments month by month.

5.q: What is a 'callable' bond?
o: One issued by a government only
One the issuer can repay early, usually when interest rates fall
One the investor can sell back at any time
5.e: Investors demand a higher yield for the risk of losing a good coupon early.

5.q: A convertible debenture…
o: Can be exchanged for the company's shares on set terms
5.e: Because of the conversion option it usually carries a lower interest rate than a plain debenture.

5.q: Which statement about the time value of money is correct?
o: Money loses no value over time
Future money is always worth more
A rupee today is worth more than a rupee promised in the future
5.e: Money today can be invested to earn a return, and the future carries uncertainty and inflation.

5.q: What does a 'stock split' of 1:5 do?
o: The dividend becomes five times larger
Each share becomes five shares at about one-fifth the price
The company raises five times more cash
5.e: Total value is unchanged; a lower price can make the share easier for small investors to buy.

5.q: An index such as the Nifty 50 measures…
o: The combined price movement of a basket of large listed companies
The price of one company's share
5.e: It is weighted by free-float market value, so larger companies move it more.

5.q: A company's 'working capital' is…
5.e: It funds day-to-day operations such as stock, wages and customer credit.

5.q: Why do lenders ask for collateral?
o: To reduce the loan amount to zero
To recover money by selling the pledged asset if the borrower defaults
5.e: Secured loans usually carry lower interest rates than unsecured ones.

5.q: A non-performing asset (NPA) for an Indian bank is a loan on which…
o: Interest or principal has been overdue for more than 90 days
5.e: High NPAs force banks to set aside provisions, cutting their profits and lending.

5.q: The SEBI rule against insider trading exists to…
o: Keep the market fair by stopping trades on unpublished price-sensitive information
5.e: Everyone should get important company news at the same time.

5.q: What does the 'margin of safety' tell a manager?
o: How far sales can fall before the business makes a loss
5.e: A larger margin of safety means the business can survive a bigger drop in demand.

5.q: When is a project accepted under the profitability index rule?
o: When the PI is less than 1
When the PI is greater than 1
5.e: PI = present value of inflows ÷ initial cost; PI > 1 is the same as NPV > 0.

5.q: A company pays out all its profit as dividends. What is its sustainable growth rate from retained earnings?
5.e: Growth from internal funds = retention ratio x ROE, and the retention ratio here is zero.

5.q: Which financial statement shows a company's position on a single date?
5.e: The profit and loss and cash flow statements cover a period, such as a year.

5.q: What is the main risk for someone who keeps all savings in a bank's savings account for 20 years?
o: Inflation may grow faster than the interest, cutting real value
5.e: Real return = nominal return - inflation (roughly); a negative real return shrinks purchasing power.

5.q: A contractor's business has assets of Rs 2,500,000 and outside liabilities of Rs 900,000. What is the owner's capital?
5.e: Accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital, so Capital = 2,500,000 - 900,000 = Rs 1,600,000.

5.q: A contractor's business has assets of Rs 780,000 and outside liabilities of Rs 310,000. What is the owner's capital?
5.e: Accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital, so Capital = 780,000 - 310,000 = Rs 470,000.

5.q: A concrete mixer costs Rs 500,000, will be sold for Rs 50,000 after 5 years. What is the yearly depreciation by the straight-line method?
5.e: (cost - salvage) ÷ life = (500,000 - 50,000) ÷ 5 = Rs 90,000 every year.

5.q: A concrete mixer costs Rs 1,200,000, will be sold for Rs 200,000 after 10 years. What is the yearly depreciation by the straight-line method?
5.e: (cost - salvage) ÷ life = (1,200,000 - 200,000) ÷ 10 = Rs 100,000 every year.

5.q: A truck bought for Rs 1,000,000 is depreciated at 20% a year on the written-down value. What is its book value after 2 years?
5.e: Book value = cost x (1 - rate)ⁿ = 1,000,000 x 0.8^2 = Rs 640,000.

5.q: A truck bought for Rs 500,000 is depreciated at 15% a year on the written-down value. What is its book value after 3 years?
5.e: Book value = cost x (1 - rate)ⁿ = 500,000 x 0.85^3 = Rs 307,062.5.

5.q: A hardware shop had opening stock of Rs 50,000, bought goods for Rs 300,000 and has closing stock of Rs 70,000. What is the cost of goods sold?
5.e: COGS = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = 50,000 + 300,000 - 70,000 = Rs 280,000.

5.q: A hardware shop had opening stock of Rs 120,000, bought goods for Rs 850,000 and has closing stock of Rs 95,000. What is the cost of goods sold?
5.e: COGS = opening stock + purchases - closing stock = 120,000 + 850,000 - 95,000 = Rs 875,000.

5.q: Sales are Rs 500,000 and the cost of goods sold is Rs 350,000. What is the gross profit margin?
Sales are Rs 1,200,000 and the cost of goods sold is Rs 900,000. What is the gross profit margin?
A firm's profits over the last 3 years were Rs 40,000, Rs 50,000, Rs 60,000. What is goodwill at 2 years' purchase of the average profit?
5.e: Average profit = Rs 50,000; goodwill = 50,000 x 2 = Rs 100,000.

5.q: A firm's profits over the last 4 years were Rs 120,000, Rs 150,000, Rs 90,000, Rs 140,000. What is goodwill at 3 years' purchase of the average profit?
5.e: Average profit = Rs 125,000; goodwill = 125,000 x 3 = Rs 375,000.

5.q: A firm earns an average profit of Rs 90,000 on capital of Rs 500,000; the normal return is 12%. What is goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit?
5.e: Normal profit = 500,000 x 12% = Rs 60,000; super profit = Rs 30,000; goodwill = 30,000 x 3 = Rs 90,000.

5.q: A firm earns an average profit of Rs 150,000 on capital of Rs 1,000,000; the normal return is 10%. What is goodwill at 2 years' purchase of super profit?
5.e: Normal profit = 1,000,000 x 10% = Rs 100,000; super profit = Rs 50,000; goodwill = 50,000 x 2 = Rs 100,000.

5.q: A partner's capital is Rs 200,000 and the deed allows 6% a year interest on capital. How much interest is credited for 12 months?
A partner's capital is Rs 150,000 and the deed allows 8% a year interest on capital. How much interest is credited for 9 months?
A company issues 10,000 shares of Rs 10 each at a premium of Rs 5. How much is credited to the Securities Premium account?
5.e: Only the premium part goes there: 10,000 x Rs 5 = Rs 50,000; 10,000 x Rs 10 goes to share capital.

5.q: A company issues 50,000 shares of Rs 10 each at a premium of Rs 15. How much is credited to the Securities Premium account?
5.e: Only the premium part goes there: 50,000 x Rs 15 = Rs 750,000; 50,000 x Rs 10 goes to share capital.

5.q: A new batching plant cost Rs 1,200,000 and earns a profit of Rs 180,000 a year. What is its return on investment?
5.e: ROI = profit ÷ investment = 180,000 ÷ 1,200,000 = 15%.

5.q: A new batching plant cost Rs 250,000 and earns a profit of Rs 60,000 a year. What is its return on investment?
5.e: ROI = profit ÷ investment = 60,000 ÷ 250,000 = 24%.

5.q: Sales are Rs 1,000,000 and variable costs are Rs 600,000. What is the profit-volume (P/V) ratio?
5.e: P/V ratio = contribution ÷ sales = 400,000 ÷ 1,000,000 = 40%.

5.q: Sales are Rs 500,000 and variable costs are Rs 350,000. What is the profit-volume (P/V) ratio?
5.e: P/V ratio = contribution ÷ sales = 150,000 ÷ 500,000 = 30%.

5.q: Fixed costs are Rs 300,000 and the P/V ratio is 40%. What sales value is needed to break even?
5.e: Break-even sales = fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio = 300,000 ÷ 0.4 = Rs 750,000.

5.q: Fixed costs are Rs 450,000 and the P/V ratio is 30%. What sales value is needed to break even?
5.e: Break-even sales = fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio = 450,000 ÷ 0.3 = Rs 1,500,000.

5.q: Fixed costs are Rs 300,000, the P/V ratio is 40% and the firm wants a profit of Rs 100,000. What sales are required?
5.e: Required sales = (fixed cost + target profit) ÷ P/V = 400,000 ÷ 0.4 = Rs 1,000,000.

5.q: Fixed costs are Rs 200,000, the P/V ratio is 25% and the firm wants a profit of Rs 50,000. What sales are required?
5.e: Required sales = (fixed cost + target profit) ÷ P/V = 250,000 ÷ 0.25 = Rs 1,000,000.

5.q: Cement has a standard price of Rs 350 a bag but was bought at Rs 365 a bag; 2,000 bags were bought. What is the size of the material price variance?
5.e: (standard price - actual price) x actual quantity = (350 - 365) x 2,000 = Rs 30,000 adverse.

5.q: Cement has a standard price of Rs 400 a bag but was bought at Rs 380 a bag; 1,500 bags were bought. What is the size of the material price variance?
5.e: (standard price - actual price) x actual quantity = (400 - 380) x 1,500 = Rs 30,000 favourable.

5.q: A slab should use 20 tonnes of steel at a standard Rs 60,000 a tonne but used 22 tonnes. What is the size of the material usage variance?
5.e: (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (20 - 22) x 60,000 = Rs 120,000 adverse.

5.q: A slab should use 50 tonnes of steel at a standard Rs 55,000 a tonne but used 48 tonnes. What is the size of the material usage variance?
5.e: (standard quantity - actual quantity) x standard price = (50 - 48) x 55,000 = Rs 110,000 favourable.

5.q: Masons are paid Rs 130 an hour against a standard rate of Rs 120; they worked 800 hours. What is the size of the labour rate variance?
5.e: (standard rate - actual rate) x actual hours = (120 - 130) x 800 = Rs 8,000 adverse.

5.q: Masons are paid Rs 85 an hour against a standard rate of Rs 90; they worked 1,200 hours. What is the size of the labour rate variance?
5.e: (standard rate - actual rate) x actual hours = (90 - 85) x 1,200 = Rs 6,000 favourable.

5.q: A workshop's budgeted overheads are Rs 600,000 for 12,000 machine hours. What is the overhead absorption rate per machine hour?
5.e: Rate = budgeted overheads ÷ budgeted hours = 600,000 ÷ 12,000 = Rs 50 per hour.

5.q: A workshop's budgeted overheads are Rs 280,000 for 3,500 machine hours. What is the overhead absorption rate per machine hour?
5.e: Rate = budgeted overheads ÷ budgeted hours = 280,000 ÷ 3,500 = Rs 80 per hour.

5.q: A dealer adds a 25% mark-up on cost. What is the profit as a percentage of the selling price (the margin)?
5.e: Margin = mark-up ÷ (100 + mark-up) = 25 ÷ 125 = 20%.

5.q: A dealer adds a 50% mark-up on cost. What is the profit as a percentage of the selling price (the margin)?
5.e: Margin = mark-up ÷ (100 + mark-up) = 50 ÷ 150 = 33.33%.

5.q: An item listed at Rs 10,000 gets a 20% trade discount and then a 5% cash discount for prompt payment. What is paid?
5.e: 10,000 x 0.8 x 0.95 = Rs 7,600 - discounts in a chain do not simply add.

5.q: An item listed at Rs 50,000 gets a 10% trade discount and then a 2% cash discount for prompt payment. What is paid?
5.e: 50,000 x 0.9 x 0.98 = Rs 44,100 - discounts in a chain do not simply add.

5.q: A tool sells for Rs 1,180 including 18% GST. What is its price before GST?
5.e: Base = inclusive price ÷ (1 + rate) = 1,180 ÷ 1.18 = Rs 1,000.

5.q: A tool sells for Rs 11,200 including 12% GST. What is its price before GST?
5.e: Base = inclusive price ÷ (1 + rate) = 11,200 ÷ 1.12 = Rs 10,000.

5.q: A bridge-deck activity has optimistic, most likely and pessimistic times of 4, 6 and 14 days. What is its PERT expected time?
A bridge-deck activity has optimistic, most likely and pessimistic times of 10, 12 and 20 days. What is its PERT expected time?
An activity's optimistic time is 4 days and pessimistic time is 16 days. What is its PERT standard deviation?
An activity's optimistic time is 6 days and pessimistic time is 24 days. What is its PERT standard deviation?
A project network has these paths - A-B-D: 4 + 6 + 5 days; A-C-D: 4 + 9 + 5 days; A-E: 4 + 12 days. What is the minimum time to finish the project?
5.e: The longest path is critical: 18 days. Any delay on it delays the whole project.

5.q: A project network has these paths - piling-pier-deck: 20 + 15 + 30 days; piling-abutment-deck: 20 + 25 + 30 days; approach road: 40 + 35 days. What is the minimum time to finish the project?
5.e: The longest path is critical: 75 days. Any delay on it delays the whole project.

5.q: An activity lasting 12 days can start at the earliest on day 10 and must finish by day 30 at the latest. What is its total float?
5.e: Total float = LF - ES - duration = 30 - 10 - 12 = 8 days.

5.q: An activity lasting 18 days can start at the earliest on day 20 and must finish by day 45 at the latest. What is its total float?
5.e: Total float = LF - ES - duration = 45 - 20 - 18 = 7 days.

5.q: A site uses at most 40 bags of cement a day and delivery takes at most 6 days. What reorder level avoids running out?
5.e: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 40 x 6 = 240 bags.

5.q: A site uses at most 25 bags of cement a day and delivery takes at most 8 days. What reorder level avoids running out?
5.e: Reorder level = maximum usage x maximum lead time = 25 x 8 = 200 bags.

5.q: Daily usage averages 35 units but can reach 50; lead time is 6 days. What safety stock covers the peak?
5.e: (maximum - average usage) x lead time = (50 - 35) x 6 = 90 units.

5.q: Daily usage averages 60 units but can reach 80; lead time is 5 days. What safety stock covers the peak?
5.e: (maximum - average usage) x lead time = (80 - 60) x 5 = 100 units.

5.q: A cube-strength test has a process mean of 30 MPa and a standard deviation of 2 MPa. What is the upper control limit (3-sigma)?
5.e: UCL = mean + 3σ = 30 + 3 x 2 = 36 MPa; the LCL is 24 MPa.

5.q: A cube-strength test has a process mean of 40 MPa and a standard deviation of 2.5 MPa. What is the upper control limit (3-sigma)?
5.e: UCL = mean + 3σ = 40 + 3 x 2.5 = 47.5 MPa; the LCL is 32.5 MPa.

5.q: A rebar diameter must lie between 11.8 and 12.2 mm; the process standard deviation is 0.05 mm. What is the process capability index Cp?
5.e: Cp = (USL - LSL) ÷ 6σ = 0.4 ÷ 0.3 = 1.33; above 1.33 is usually considered capable.

5.q: A rebar diameter must lie between 24.5 and 25.5 mm; the process standard deviation is 0.1 mm. What is the process capability index Cp?
5.e: Cp = (USL - LSL) ÷ 6σ = 1 ÷ 0.6 = 1.67; above 1.33 is usually considered capable.

5.q: A crushing plant has 90% availability, 95% performance and 99% quality rate. What is its overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)?
5.e: OEE = availability x performance x quality = 0.9 x 0.95 x 0.99 = 84.64%.

5.q: A crushing plant has 85% availability, 90% performance and 98% quality rate. What is its overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)?
5.e: OEE = availability x performance x quality = 0.85 x 0.9 x 0.98 = 74.97%.

5.q: A crew of 6 workers lays 1,800 paver blocks in a 8-hour shift. What is the labour productivity per worker-hour?
5.e: Output ÷ input = 1,800 ÷ (6 x 8) = 37.5 blocks per worker-hour.

5.q: A crew of 8 workers lays 2,400 paver blocks in a 10-hour shift. What is the labour productivity per worker-hour?
5.e: Output ÷ input = 2,400 ÷ (8 x 10) = 30 blocks per worker-hour.

5.q: When the price of a road-toll pass rises by 10%, the number of passes sold falls by 30%. What is the size of the price elasticity of demand?
5.e: |%ΔQ ÷ %ΔP| = 30 ÷ 10 = 3; elastic (above 1): raising the price lowers revenue.

5.q: When the price of a road-toll pass rises by 10%, the number of passes sold falls by 5%. What is the size of the price elasticity of demand?
5.e: |%ΔQ ÷ %ΔP| = 5 ÷ 10 = 0.5; inelastic (below 1): raising the price raises revenue.

5.q: A construction firm started the year with 80 engineers and ended with 88; 12 left during the year. What is the attrition rate?
5.e: Leavers ÷ average headcount = 12 ÷ 84 = 14.29%.

5.q: A construction firm started the year with 140 engineers and ended with 160; 30 left during the year. What is the attrition rate?
5.e: Leavers ÷ average headcount = 30 ÷ 150 = 20%.

5.q: The going-concern concept assumes that a business…
o: Will continue operating for the foreseeable future
Will close at the end of the year
5.e: That is why fixed assets are shown at cost less depreciation rather than at forced-sale value.

5.q: Which principle says expenses should be recorded in the same period as the revenue they help earn?
5.e: So wages for March's work belong to March's profit even if they are paid in April.

5.q: The prudence (conservatism) concept means…
o: Anticipate no profits but provide for all likely losses
5.e: Stock is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value for this reason.

5.q: Under the dual-aspect concept, every transaction…
o: Is recorded twice in the same account
Has two equal effects, so the accounting equation always balances
5.e: This is the basis of double-entry book-keeping: total debits always equal total credits.

5.q: Buying a new crane for a construction company is…
5.e: It brings benefit over many years, so it is shown as an asset and depreciated; its fuel is revenue expenditure.

5.q: Which error will NOT be revealed by a trial balance?
o: Posting only one side of an entry
Posting a debit to the credit side
A wrong total in a ledger account
5.e: If a transaction is left out entirely, debits and credits still match; errors of principle and compensating errors also hide.

5.q: Why does a bank reconciliation statement need to be prepared?
o: The cash book and bank passbook balances differ because of timing and errors
5.e: Cheques issued but not yet presented, or bank charges not yet recorded, are common reasons.

5.q: How does a provision differ from a reserve?
o: A reserve is a charge against profit
A provision covers a known liability or loss; a reserve is profit set aside
5.e: Provision for doubtful debts is charged against profit; a general reserve is an appropriation of profit.

5.q: If a partnership deed is silent, how are profits shared under the Indian Partnership Act?
5.e: Without a deed there is also no interest on capital and no salary for partners; loans from partners earn 6% a year.

5.q: When a new partner joins and brings goodwill in cash, the old partners share it in…
5.e: Sacrificing ratio = old share - new share for each old partner.

5.q: Preference shareholders differ from equity shareholders because they…
o: Get a fixed dividend first and are repaid before equity on winding up
Always control the company by voting
5.e: Equity holders bear the most risk but keep all remaining profits and normally hold the votes.

5.q: Debenture holders of a company are its…
o: Creditors, entitled to interest whether or not there is profit
5.e: Debenture interest is a charge against profit; dividends are paid out of profit.

5.q: In a cash flow statement, buying a new machine is shown under…
5.e: Operating covers day-to-day trading; financing covers loans, share issues and dividends.

5.q: Which cost stays the same in total when output rises (within a range)?
o: Fixed cost, such as site office rent
Variable cost, such as cement per cubic metre
5.e: Fixed cost per unit falls as output rises; variable cost per unit stays constant.

5.q: In marginal costing, which costs are charged to products?
o: Only variable costs; fixed costs are written off in the period
5.e: This makes short-term decisions such as accepting a special order clearer.

5.q: A firm with spare capacity gets a special order below its normal price. It should usually accept if…
o: The price covers full cost including fixed overheads
The price is below variable cost
The price is above the variable cost per unit
5.e: Fixed costs are paid anyway, so any contribution adds to profit - provided normal sales are not harmed.

5.q: What is standard costing mainly used for?
o: Comparing actual costs with predetermined standards to find variances
5.e: Analysing price and usage variances shows managers where to act.

5.q: In ABC inventory analysis, 'A' items are…
o: A few items that make up most of the total value
5.e: A items (about 10-20% of items, 70-80% of value) get the tightest control; C items the least.

5.q: The just-in-time (JIT) approach aims to…
o: Receive materials exactly when needed, keeping inventory minimal
Produce as much as possible regardless of demand
5.e: It cuts storage cost and waste but needs very reliable suppliers.

5.q: Kaizen means…
5.e: The Japanese idea builds quality and productivity step by step from the shop floor up.

5.q: A Six Sigma process aims for about how many defects per million opportunities?
5.e: It allows for a 1.5σ drift of the mean; the method uses the DMAIC cycle.

5.q: A point outside the 3-sigma limits of a control chart usually signals…
o: An assignable (special) cause that should be investigated
5.e: Random variation alone puts only about 3 points in 1,000 outside the limits.

5.q: The critical path in a project network is…
o: The longest path, with zero total float
5.e: Shortening the project means shortening (crashing) activities on this path.

5.q: 'Crashing' an activity in project scheduling means…
o: Doing it after the project ends
Shortening its duration by adding resources, at extra cost
5.e: Crash the critical activity with the lowest cost per day saved first.

5.q: How does PERT differ from CPM?
o: CPM is only for research projects
PERT uses three time estimates for uncertain activities; CPM uses one fixed time
5.e: PERT suits new, uncertain work such as research; CPM suits repetitive construction where times are well known.

5.q: A Gantt chart shows…
o: Activities as bars against a time scale
5.e: It is easy to read but does not show dependencies as clearly as a network diagram.

5.q: Fayol's principle of 'unity of command' says that…
o: Each employee should receive orders from only one superior
Orders should come from many managers
5.e: Two bosses giving conflicting orders cause confusion on site.

5.q: F. W. Taylor is known as the father of…
5.e: He used time and motion studies to find the 'one best way' of doing each task.

5.q: Which management function compares actual performance with plans and corrects deviations?
5.e: Planning sets the targets; controlling checks progress against them and closes the loop.

5.q: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which level comes right after physiological needs?
5.e: Order: physiological → safety → social → esteem → self-actualisation.

5.q: McGregor's Theory Y assumes that workers…
o: Like responsibility and can direct themselves
Dislike work and must be closely supervised
5.e: Theory X managers rely on control; Theory Y managers rely on participation and trust.

5.q: The four Ps of the marketing mix are…
5.e: Services add people, process and physical evidence to make seven Ps.

5.q: In which stage of the product life cycle are sales highest and competition fiercest?
5.e: Firms then compete on price and features and look for new uses or markets.

5.q: Under GST, input tax credit allows a business to…
o: Pay tax only once a decade
Deduct the GST it paid on purchases from the GST it collects on sales
5.e: Tax is then paid only on the value added at each stage, removing the 'tax on tax' cascade.

5.q: Which GST applies when goods move from one Indian state to another?
5.e: For sales within one state, CGST and SGST are charged in equal halves.

5.q: For a contract to be valid under the Indian Contract Act, which is essential?
o: It must be written on stamp paper always
It must involve a government department
Free consent of competent parties and lawful consideration
5.e: An agreement without consideration is generally void, with a few exceptions such as gifts made in writing out of natural love.

5.q: A contract signed because one party was threatened is…
o: Voidable at the option of the threatened party
5.e: Coercion, undue influence and fraud make a contract voidable; the affected party may choose to cancel it.

5.q: What is a 'crossed' cheque?
o: One that can only be paid into a bank account, not cashed over the counter
5.e: Two parallel lines across the cheque protect against theft, since the money must go to an account.

5.q: How does a private limited company differ from a public limited company in India?
o: It cannot invite the public to buy its shares
5.e: A private company can have at most 200 members; a One Person Company has a single member.

5.q: What is the main advantage of a limited liability partnership (LLP) over an ordinary partnership?
o: Partners' personal assets are protected beyond their agreed contribution
5.e: An LLP is a separate legal entity; one partner is not liable for another's misconduct.

5.q: A PESTLE analysis of the business environment examines…
o: Political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors
5.e: For a bridge contractor, new safety laws (legal) and steel prices (economic) are typical items.

5.q: In a SWOT analysis, 'opportunities' and 'threats' refer to…
5.e: Strengths and weaknesses are internal; opportunities and threats come from the environment.

5.q: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a consumer can complain about…
o: Defective goods, deficient services and unfair trade practices
5.e: Complaints go to district, state or national commissions depending on the value involved; e-commerce is also covered.

5.q: Which communication barrier is caused by using technical jargon with site workers?
5.e: The message is sent but not understood; plain words and demonstrations help.

5.q: A leader who makes decisions alone and expects obedience follows which style?
5.e: It can work in emergencies on site but often lowers morale in the long run.

5.q: Delegation of authority means…
o: Giving a subordinate the power to act, while the manager remains accountable
Passing all responsibility and accountability downwards
5.e: Authority can be delegated; ultimate accountability cannot.

5.q: Which of these is an example of a non-financial incentive?
o: Recognition and a chance of promotion
5.e: Status, job security and challenging work also motivate, often as much as money.

5.q: What does 'span of control' mean?
o: The length of a bridge span
The total budget of a department
The working hours of a manager
The number of subordinates a manager directly supervises
5.e: A narrow span means more layers of management; a wide span means a flatter organisation.

5.q: A matrix organisation is common in engineering firms because…
o: Each worker reports only to the owner
Staff report to both a functional head and a project manager
5.e: It shares specialists across projects but can create conflicts between two bosses.

5.q: Why do companies prepare a budget?
o: To plan, coordinate and control activities against targets
5.e: Budgets turn plans into numbers; comparing actuals with them shows where action is needed.

5.q: What is a flexible budget?
o: One adjusted to the actual level of activity achieved
5.e: It separates fixed and variable costs so that performance is judged at the real output level.

5.q: Under the FIFO method, closing stock is valued at…
5.e: Goods bought first are assumed to be used first, so what is left is the latest stock.

5.q: Which of these is an intangible asset?
5.e: Intangible assets have value without physical form; most are amortised over their useful life.

5.q: A contingent liability, such as a pending court case, is shown…
o: As a note to the accounts, not in the balance sheet total
5.e: It may or may not turn into a real liability; if it becomes probable, a provision is made.

5.q: Which statement about outsourcing is correct?
o: Contracting work to outside specialists so the firm can focus on its core activities
5.e: A bridge builder may outsource piling to a specialist subcontractor.

5.q: Which statement best describes an MSME in India?
o: A micro, small or medium enterprise classified by investment and turnover
5.e: MSMEs get priority-sector lending and other support, and employ a large share of India's workforce.

5.q: A tender is awarded on the L1 basis. What does L1 mean?
o: The bid with the most pages
5.e: Only bids that pass the technical evaluation are compared on price.

5.q: What does a 'bill of quantities' in a construction tender list?
o: The items of work with their quantities, to be priced by bidders
5.e: Bidders fill in rates; the totals give comparable prices and later the basis for measured payments.

5.q: Why is internal audit useful to a company?
o: It independently checks that controls work and records are reliable
5.e: Internal auditors report to management or the audit committee throughout the year.

5.q: Which type of cost should be ignored when choosing between two future options?
o: Future cash costs that differ between the options
A cost already incurred that cannot be recovered
5.e: Only relevant costs - future and different between the options - should drive the decision.

5.q: What is a 'make or buy' decision about?
o: Whether to issue shares or debentures
Whether to pay tax now or later
Whether to produce a part in-house or purchase it from a supplier
Whether to hire or fire staff
5.e: Compare the relevant in-house cost with the purchase price, and weigh quality and control too.

5.q: A company holds too little inventory. Which cost rises?
o: Stock-out (shortage) costs such as idle crews and lost sales
5.e: Holding costs rise with more stock; ordering and shortage costs rise with less. The EOQ balances them.

5.q: Which document is the formal request from a buyer to a supplier to supply goods?
5.e: The supplier then sends goods with a delivery challan and bills with an invoice.

5.q: Which account is credited when a business receives cash from a customer who owed it money?
5.e: Cash (an asset) increases and is debited; the debtor's balance falls and is credited.

5.q: Goods withdrawn by the owner for personal use are recorded as…
5.e: Drawings account is debited and purchases (or stock) is credited at cost.

5.q: Accrued (outstanding) wages at year end are shown in the balance sheet as…
5.e: The work was done this year, so the cost belongs to this year even though it is paid next year.

5.q: Rent paid in advance for next year is shown as…
o: A prepaid expense, a current asset
5.e: The benefit has not yet been received, so it is carried forward as an asset.

5.q: A provision for doubtful debts is created because of which concept?
5.e: Some customers may not pay; recognising the likely loss now avoids overstating profit and assets.

5.q: When a partner retires, the remaining partners acquire his share in…
5.e: Gaining ratio = new share - old share; they compensate the retiring partner for goodwill in this ratio.

5.q: Forfeiture of shares happens when…
o: A shareholder fails to pay calls due on the shares
5.e: The amount already received is kept in a forfeited shares account; the shares can be reissued.

5.q: What is the purpose of a 'suspense account' when a trial balance does not agree?
o: To hold the difference temporarily until the errors are found
5.e: As each error is found and corrected, the suspense account is cleared to zero.

5.q: Which of these is an example of a fictitious asset?
o: Preliminary expenses not yet written off
5.e: It has no real value; modern standards require such costs to be expensed rather than carried as assets.

5.q: What does a 'contribution' in marginal costing cover?
5.e: Contribution = sales - variable cost; once fixed costs are covered, every extra rupee of contribution is profit.

5.q: A 'key factor' (limiting factor) in production planning is…
o: The scarce resource that restricts output, such as machine hours
5.e: When a factor is scarce, rank products by contribution per unit of that factor.

5.q: Which statement about economies of scale is correct?
o: Average cost per unit falls as output grows, up to a point
Small firms always have lower costs
5.e: Bulk buying and specialised machinery spread fixed costs; too large a scale can bring diseconomies.

5.q: A 5S programme on a site aims to…
o: Organise the workplace: sort, set in order, shine, standardise, sustain
5.e: A tidy, well-organised site is safer and wastes less time searching for tools.

5.q: Which statement about a sole proprietorship is correct?
o: It is a separate legal entity
The owner has unlimited personal liability for business debts
It must have at least seven members
5.e: It is the simplest form of business, but the owner's personal assets are at risk.

5.q: What is 'e-procurement' in public works?
o: Buying goods and services through online tendering platforms
5.e: India's Central Public Procurement Portal and GeM make bidding more transparent and competitive.

5.q: What does 'quality assurance' focus on, compared with 'quality control'?
o: Preventing defects through good processes, rather than finding them after production
5.e: QA designs the system right; QC inspects the output. Both are needed on a bridge site.

5.q: Two parallel members with stiffness 70 and 45 kN/mm share a 450 kN load. How much does the first carry?
Two parallel members with stiffness 10 and 80 kN/mm share a 1450 kN load. How much does the first carry?
A bridge mode has stiffness 100000 N/m and mass 5000 kg. What is its natural frequency?
A bridge mode has stiffness 1e+06 N/m and mass 2000 kg. What is its natural frequency?
An undamped bridge is shaken at 0.8 times its natural frequency. By what factor is the static deflection amplified?
5.e: Dynamic amplification = 1/|1 - r²| = 2.78; near r = 1 it explodes (resonance).

5.q: An undamped bridge is shaken at 2 times its natural frequency. By what factor is the static deflection amplified?
5.e: Dynamic amplification = 1/|1 - r²| = 0.333; near r = 1 it explodes (resonance).

5.q: A stay carries 4600 kN. Using strengths of 1500 MPa (steel) and 2400 MPa (carbon fibre), how much less area does carbon need?
5.e: Steel 3067 mm², carbon 1917 mm²; difference 1150 mm².

5.q: A stay carries 2700 kN. Using strengths of 1500 MPa (steel) and 2400 MPa (carbon fibre), how much less area does carbon need?
5.e: Steel 1800 mm², carbon 1125 mm²; difference 675 mm².

5.q: A convoy of 3 trucks of 45 t each crosses with impact factor 1.2. What total design load? (g = 9.81)
A convoy of 3 trucks of 30 t each crosses with impact factor 1.3. What total design load? (g = 9.81)
Two members joined side by side share a load in proportion to their:
5.e: The stiffer one takes more: F1 = F k1/(k1 + k2).

5.q: Resonance is dangerous when the forcing frequency is:
o: Much lower than all natural frequencies
5.e: The response can grow huge without damping.

5.q: Dampers make a bridge safer by:
5.e: Tuned mass and viscous dampers absorb energy.

5.q: The London Millennium Bridge wobbled in 2000 because:
o: People walking in step matched its sideways sway
5.e: It was fixed with 91 dampers.

5.q: How many neutrons are in Ca-40 (Z = 20)?
5.e: Neutrons = A - Z = 40 - 20 = 20.

5.q: Lanthanoid contraction makes Zr and Hf:
5.e: Poor shielding by 4f electrons.

5.q: Which gas causes the greenhouse effect most among these?
5.e: CO2 absorbs infrared radiation.

5.q: Haber process makes ammonia using an iron catalyst at about:
5.e: A compromise between yield and rate.

5.q: Fayol's 'unity of command' means:
o: One plan for the whole firm
An employee gets orders from one boss only
5.e: Two bosses cause confusion.

5.q: SEBI was set up to:
o: Regulate the securities market and protect investors
5.e: Securities and Exchange Board of India, statutory since 1992.

5.q: ACID in databases stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and:
5.e: Committed transactions survive crashes.

5.q: Two's complement of a binary number is:
5.e: It represents negative numbers so addition just works.

5.q: Pipelining in a CPU improves:
5.e: Stages overlap so one instruction finishes every cycle (ideally).

5.q: The halting problem is:
5.e: Turing proved no program can decide halting for all programs.

5.q: If a problem in NP-complete gets a polynomial-time algorithm, then:
5.e: Every NP problem reduces to an NP-complete one.

5.q: What is hexadecimal EAC in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: EAC (base 16) = 3756.

5.q: What is hexadecimal 6CD in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: 6CD (base 16) = 1741.

5.q: A = 1, B = 0, C = 1. What is the output of (A OR B) AND C?
5.e: A OR B = 1; then 1 AND 1 = 1.

5.q: What is hexadecimal DB6 in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: DB6 (base 16) = 3510.

5.q: What is hexadecimal 3FB in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: 3FB (base 16) = 1019.

5.q: What is hexadecimal D8E in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: D8E (base 16) = 3470.

5.q: A = 0, B = 0, C = 1. What is the output of (A AND B) XNOR C?
5.e: A AND B = 0; then 0 XNOR 1 = 0.

5.q: What is hexadecimal A2E in decimal?
5.e: Each hex digit is a power of 16: A2E (base 16) = 2606.

5.q: Revenue grew from ₹210 crore to ₹255.5 crore in 5 years. What is the compound annual growth rate?
5.e: CAGR = (end / start)^(1/5) - 1 = 4%; simple averaging overstates it.

5.q: Revenue grew from ₹370 crore to ₹652.1 crore in 5 years. What is the compound annual growth rate?
5.e: CAGR = (end / start)^(1/5) - 1 = 12%; simple averaging overstates it.

5.q: Real interest rate is approximately:
5.e: Fisher relation: (1 + r)(1 + pi) = 1 + i.

5.q: WACC is used as the:
o: Discount rate for a firm's projects
5.e: Weighted average cost of capital blends debt and equity costs.

5.q: Price elasticity of demand above 1 (in size) means demand is:
5.e: Quantity changes more than price in percentage terms.

5.q: The order of the differential equation y'' + 3y' + 2y = 0 is:
5.e: Highest derivative present.

5.q: The mean of a binomial distribution B(n, p) is:
5.e: Variance is npq.

5.q: The angle between two vectors with zero dot product is:
5.e: a·b = |a||b|cos θ = 0.

5.q: Bernoulli's principle is a statement of conservation of:
5.e: P + ½ρv² + ρgh is constant along a streamline.

5.q: The speed of sound in a gas is proportional to:
5.e: v = √(γRT/M).

5.q: Which of these is NOT an electromagnetic wave?
5.e: Sound is a mechanical wave.

5.q: A ball is projected at 20 m/s from the foot of a fixed incline of 30°. What is the maximum range it can have up the incline? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: R_max (up the incline) = u² ÷ [g(1 + sin β)] = 20² ÷ [10 x (1 + 0.5)] = 26.67 m, at θ = 45° + β/2 from the horizontal.

5.q: A ball is projected at 30 m/s from the foot of a fixed incline of 37°. What is the maximum range it can have up the incline? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: R_max (up the incline) = u² ÷ [g(1 + sin β)] = 30² ÷ [10 x (1 + 0.6)] = 56.25 m, at θ = 45° + β/2 from the horizontal.

5.q: A 4 kg block on a horizontal table (friction coefficient 0.2) is tied over a light pulley to a hanging 2 kg block. What is the acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: a = (m₂g - μm₁g) ÷ (m₁ + m₂) = (20 - 8) ÷ 6 = 2 m/s².

5.q: A 3 kg block on a horizontal table (friction coefficient 0.25) is tied over a light pulley to a hanging 3 kg block. What is the acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
A 2 kg block rests on a 3 kg plank on a frictionless floor; the friction coefficient between them is 0.4. What is the largest horizontal force on the PLANK for which they move together? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: Friction can give the top block at most a = μg = 4 m/s²; F = (m₁ + m₂) μg = 5 x 4 = 20 N.

5.q: A 1 kg block rests on a 4 kg plank on a frictionless floor; the friction coefficient between them is 0.3. What is the largest horizontal force on the PLANK for which they move together? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: Friction can give the top block at most a = μg = 3 m/s²; F = (m₁ + m₂) μg = 5 x 3 = 15 N.

5.q: A bob on a string of length 0.8 m must just complete a vertical circle. What is the minimum speed needed at the lowest point? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: At the top tension can be zero, so v_top = √(gR); energy then gives v_bottom = √(5gR) = √(50 x 0.8) = 6.32 m/s.

5.q: A bob on a string of length 2 m must just complete a vertical circle. What is the minimum speed needed at the lowest point? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: At the top tension can be zero, so v_top = √(gR); energy then gives v_bottom = √(5gR) = √(50 x 2) = 10 m/s.

5.q: A 0.5 kg bob just completes a vertical circle on a string. What is the string tension at the lowest point? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: T = mg + mv²/R with v² = 5gR, so T = 6mg = 6 x 0.5 x 10 = 30 N - independent of the radius.

5.q: A 2 kg bob just completes a vertical circle on a string. What is the string tension at the lowest point? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: T = mg + mv²/R with v² = 5gR, so T = 6mg = 6 x 2 x 10 = 120 N - independent of the radius.

5.q: A 5,000 kg rocket ejects gas at 50 kg/s with exhaust speed 2,000 m/s relative to it. What is its initial upward acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
A 2,000 kg rocket ejects gas at 20 kg/s with exhaust speed 1,500 m/s relative to it. What is its initial upward acceleration? (g = 10 m/s²)
From a uniform disc of radius 12 cm, a circular hole of radius 6 cm is cut so that it touches the rim. How far does the centre of mass move from the disc's centre?
5.e: The hole has 1/4 of the mass at distance R/2: x = (1/4 x R/2) ÷ (1 - 1/4) = R/6 = 2 cm, away from the hole.

5.q: From a uniform disc of radius 30 cm, a circular hole of radius 15 cm is cut so that it touches the rim. How far does the centre of mass move from the disc's centre?
5.e: The hole has 1/4 of the mass at distance R/2: x = (1/4 x R/2) ÷ (1 - 1/4) = R/6 = 5 cm, away from the hole.

5.q: A solid ball is launched sliding (not spinning) at 7 m/s on a floor with friction coefficient 0.2. After how long does it start rolling without slipping? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: Friction slows v (a = μg) and spins it up (α = 5μg/2R); v = ωR when t = 2v₀ ÷ 7μg = 1 s, when v = 5v₀/7.

5.q: A solid ball is launched sliding (not spinning) at 14 m/s on a floor with friction coefficient 0.1. After how long does it start rolling without slipping? (g = 10 m/s²)
5.e: Friction slows v (a = μg) and spins it up (α = 5μg/2R); v = ωR when t = 2v₀ ÷ 7μg = 4 s, when v = 5v₀/7.
